summary: Source decomposition of four primary works for the integral local theory of finite flat group schemes: Raynaud, Schemas en groupes de type (p,...,p) (1974); Fontaine-Laffaille, Construction de representations p-adiques (1982); Kisin, Moduli of finite flat group schemes, and modularity (2009) Section 1 and 2.2.16-2.2.22; Liu, Barsotti-Tate groups and Kisin modules when p = 2 (2013). Also used: Fontaine, Il n'y a pas de variete abelienne sur Z (1985) Sections 1-2, and Conrad, Finite group schemes over bases with low ramification (1999, public author copy) for written expositions of results that Raynaud and Fontaine-Laffaille only recall. R07.1 covers all of Raynaud Sections 1-4 and the appendix: the classification of F-vector space schemes, prolongations over a DVR, uniqueness for e < p-1, tame characters (Theorems 3.4.1, 3.4.3, Corollary 3.4.4) and the determinant Theorem 4.1.1. The last is the node the Faltings packet cites. Raynaud Corollaries 3.3.6-3.3.7 have no written proof; this is recorded. R07.3 follows Fontaine-Laffaille Sections 1-9: the torsion category and ring S, Theorem 3.3, simple objects and the tame computation (Theorem 5.3), the endpoint collision (0.9), full faithfulness on MF' (proved) and MF'' (only indicated), strongly divisible lattices, Theorem 8.4, and the Honda-system dictionary with J(Abar) = U_S(M). R07.4 covers Kisin's Breuil/Kisin-module formalism for p > 2 with k finite (Breuil's theorem imported), his p-divisible group classification, and Liu's proof for all p including p = 2. R07.6 covers Fontaine's ramification bound (Theorem A/1, with the G^(u) = G^{u-1} convention) with all of Section 1, and Raynaud's det T(X) = tau^d. R07.2 and R07.5 are covered only at statement level (Dieudonne theory) or by one example (supersingular E[p]). Every stage stays partial: Tate 1967, Serre 1972, Breuil 2000, Fontaine's Asterisque volumes, Laffaille 1980, Kisin 2006 and the Grothendieck-Messing sources are absent, and several roadmap targets (descent data, Serre-Tate, Tate shifts, ordinary inertia) are not in the sources read.

nodes.title: Fundamental characters of a finite field and the p-adic writing of characters
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, r >= 1, q = p^r and F a field with q elements. Let C be the subfield of Qbar generated by the (q-1)-th roots of unity, D' the integral closure of Z in C, P a place of D' above p, and D the Dedekind ring of the open subscheme of Spec(D') obtained by inverting q-1 and removing the points above p other than P. Let M be the group of characters chi : F^* -> mu_{q-1}(D), extended by chi(0) = 0. A character chi in M is fundamental if the composite F -> D -> k(P) is a field homomorphism (equivalently, is additive). The fundamental characters form one orbit chi_i under chi -> chi^p, indexed by a principal homogeneous space under Z/rZ with chi_i^p = chi_{i+1}. Every chi in M has a p-adic writing chi = prod_i chi_i^{n_i} with 0 <= n_i <= p-1, unique except for chi = 1, which is both n_i = 0 for all i and n_i = p-1 for all i. If P' = sigma(P) is another place above p (sigma in Gal(C/Q)), the characters fundamental at P' are the sigma o chi_i; every primitive character of F^* is fundamental at exactly one place of D' above p (Remark 1.1.2).
hypotheses: p prime, q = p^r with r >= 1, F a finite field with q elements
D is the ring of integers of Q(mu_{q-1}) with q-1 inverted and localized away from the places above p other than the chosen place P; the notion of fundamental character depends on P
proofSteps: Take M = Hom(F^*, mu_{q-1}(D)), a cyclic group of order q-1, and extend characters to F by chi(0) = 0.

Since k(P) has q elements, a character chi whose reduction F -> k(P) is additive is a field isomorphism F -> k(P); composing with the Frobenius of k(P) gives the other such characters chi^{p^h}, and chi^{p^r} = chi, so the fundamental characters are indexed by Z/rZ with chi_i^p = chi_{i+1}.

Every character of the cyclic group F^* is a power of a fundamental character chi_i; writing the exponent in base p gives the p-adic writing prod_i chi_i^{n_i}, and the only non-uniqueness is n_i = 0 for all i versus n_i = p-1 for all i, both giving chi = 1 because chi_i^{(p^r-1)/(p-1) (p-1)} = 1.
Remark 1.1.2: Gal(C/Q) = (Z/(q-1)Z)^* permutes the places above p, and sigma(P) = P' carries the fundamental characters at P to those at P'.
acceptance: For r = 1 there is a single fundamental character: the Teichmueller-type character F_p^* -> mu_{p-1}(D) reducing to the identity modulo P.
Check the non-uniqueness of the p-adic writing at chi = 1 and nowhere else.

Record that Raynaud flags a small terminological difference from Serre [12], p. 267 (N.B. after Definition 1.1.1), so Serre's fundamental characters must be matched before importing Serre 1972 results.

nodes.title: Schemes in F-vector spaces, the eigensheaf decomposition of the augmentation ideal, and condition (**)
nodes.statement: For a scheme S, an S-functor in F-vector spaces is a contravariant functor (Sch/S)^op -> (F-vector spaces); when representable it is an S-scheme in F-vector spaces. Assume it is finite, flat and of finite presentation over S. Its underlying commutative group scheme G is killed by p, and the Cartier dual G' = Hom_gr(G, G_m) is an S-scheme in F-vector spaces via (lambda u)(x) = u(lambda x) (the dual of V). The F-structure is equivalent to bialgebra endomorphisms [lambda] of the bialgebra A of G with [lambda] o [mu] = [lambda mu] and d o ([lambda] (x) [mu]) o c = [lambda + mu]. Under hypothesis (*), S is a scheme over Spec(D) (notation of 1.1). The endomorphisms e_chi = (1/(q-1)) sum_{lambda in F^*} chi^{-1}(lambda)[lambda], chi in M, are orthogonal idempotents preserving the augmentation ideal I, giving a canonical decomposition I = direct sum over chi in M of I_chi, where I_chi is the set of a with [lambda]a = chi(lambda)a. This makes A an M-graded bialgebra. Condition (**) requires each I_chi to be an invertible O_S-module; A then has constant rank q. Proposition 1.2.2 gives (**) when G is defined by a bialgebra of rank q, S is connected, and some fibre G_s is etale or of multiplicative type. This holds in particular when S is integral with fraction field of characteristic zero.
hypotheses: (*): S is a D-scheme, so that each chi in M gives a character F^* -> mu_{q-1}(S)
G finite, flat, of finite presentation over S
for Proposition 1.2.2: rank of the bialgebra equal to q, S connected, and one fibre etale or of multiplicative type
proofSteps: Translate the functoriality [lambda] o [mu] = [lambda mu] and the distributivity d o ([lambda] (x) [mu]) o c = [lambda + mu] (formulas (2)-(3), p. 245) into the idempotent decomposition of I, and transport it to the dual bialgebra A'.
Proof of Proposition 1.2.2: I_chi is a direct summand of the locally free module A, hence locally free, of constant rank because S is connected; it suffices to see rank 1 at the given point s.

At s, after replacing G by its Cartier dual and s by a geometric point, G is constant etale over a field k and G(k) is an F-vector space of rank 1 (rank q). A is then the bialgebra of k-valued functions on F, and each I_chi is spanned by e_chi = sum_a chi(a) epsilon_a (computed explicitly in 1.3).
acceptance: Remark 1.2.3: over a field k containing F, the product of r copies of alpha_p is an F-vector space scheme of rank q whose eigensheaves are not of rank 1 for r > 1, so (**) is a genuine restriction.
For r = 1 and S over Z_p[mu_{p-1}], check that mu_p and Z/pZ satisfy (**) (the Oort-Tate situation cited as [10]).

nodes.title: The universal structure constants w_chi and w, their Gauss-sum formula and p-adic valuations
nodes.statement: For G satisfying (**) and characters chi_1, ..., chi_n in M, the composite d_{chi_1,...,chi_n} o c_{chi_1,...,chi_n} of iterated multiplication and comultiplication on the invertible sheaf I_{chi_1...chi_n} is multiplication by a universal constant w_{chi_1,...,chi_n} in D, independent of G. These constants satisfy the associativity formula (7). For two characters, (10) gives w_{chi_1,chi_2} = ((chi_1 chi_2)(-1)/(q-1)) j(chi_1^{-1}, chi_2^{-1}) when chi_1, chi_2 are nontrivial, where j is the Jacobi sum; (10 bis) and (10 ter) give w_{1,chi} = w_{chi,1} = w_{1,1} = -q/(q-1). Comparison with the constant group of F^+ and its Cartier dual gives (14): w_{chi_1,...,chi_n} = (1/(q-1)^{n-1}) g(chi_1)...g(chi_n)/g(chi_1...chi_n), where g(1) = -q and g(chi) = sum_{a in F} chi^{-1}(a) psi(a) is the Gauss sum for a nontrivial additive character psi. Consequently (15) w_{chi_1,...,chi_n} w_{chi_1^{-1},...,chi_n^{-1}} = (q/(q-1)^2)^{n-1} when all chi_j are nontrivial, and (16) w is invariant under chi -> chi^p, so the constants lie in the Frobenius-invariant subring D_1. Proposition 1.3.1: (1) for chi = prod_i chi_i^{a_i} written p-adically (0 <= a_i <= p-1, not all zero), w_chi := w_{chi_1,...,chi_1,...,chi_r,...,chi_r} (chi_i repeated a_i times) is a unit of D_1 with w_chi = a_1! ... a_r! (mod p); (2) w := w_i = d_i o c_i, the constant for chi_i^p = chi_{i+1} (independent of i by (16)), satisfies w = p! (mod p^2) and w = p u with u a unit of D_1, u = -1 (mod p).
hypotheses: G satisfies (**) over a D-scheme S; the constants are computed in D
psi a nontrivial additive character of F with values in mu_p(Dtilde), Dtilde the integral closure of D in C(mu_p); for (16) psi is the trace to Z/pZ followed by a nontrivial character
proofSteps: Restrict the distributivity (3) to I_chi to obtain (8), then multiply by chi_1^{-1}(lambda) chi_2^{-1}(mu) and sum over lambda, mu in F^* to obtain (9) and the three cases (10), (10 bis), (10 ter).

Section 1.3: for the constant group G on F^+ over D, the characteristic functions epsilon_a give e_chi = sum_a chi(a) epsilon_a with e_chi^p = e_{chi^p} (12); the dual A' is the group algebra of F^+ with basis dual to (epsilon_a), giving (12 bis).

A nontrivial additive character psi defines a Dtilde-morphism of F-vector space schemes G -> G' whose bialgebra map sends e_chi to g(chi) epsilon_chi (13); comparing (12) and (12 bis) gives w_{chi',chi''} = g(chi')g(chi'')/((q-1) g(chi' chi'')) and, with (7), formula (14).
The classical Gauss-sum identities g(chi)g(chi^{-1}) = q chi(-1) ([14] Weil, p. 501) and g(chi^p) = g(chi) ([8] Lang, p. 93) give (15) and (16).

Proof of Proposition 1.3.1: (15) shows w_chi and w are invertible in D_1 localized at (p). The Lie algebra of G' (x) k is Hom_gr(F^+, k^+), whose F^*-eigencharacters are exactly the fundamental characters, so G' (x) k is radicial of height 1, isomorphic to mu_p^r, with A' (x) k generated by the images of e_i subject only to e_i^p = 0. Hence prod_i e_i^{a_i} is nonzero mod p while e_i^p = 0 mod p, which with (12 bis) gives that w_chi is a unit and that w = 0 mod p.

The congruence w_chi = a_1! ... a_r! mod p comes from computing the coefficient of epsilon_{chi_1}^{(x)a_1} (x) ... in the iterated coproduct of epsilon_chi, using c(epsilon_{chi_i}) = 1 (x) epsilon_{chi_i} + epsilon_{chi_i} (x) 1 mod p. The same computation for epsilon_{chi_i}^p gives w = p! mod p^2, and (p-1)! = -1 mod p gives u = -1 mod p.
acceptance: r = 1, n = 2, chi_1 = chi_2 = 1: check (10 ter) against the direct count sum_{u+v=1, u,v != 0} 1 = q-2.
Check w = p u with u = -1 mod p numerically for q = p = 3 using the Gauss sums of F_3.
Confirm that nothing in this node uses the characteristic of the base S: the constants live in D_1 and are pulled back to any D-scheme.

nodes.title: Raynaud classification of F-vector space schemes satisfying (**) by invertible sheaves with maps c_i, d_i, d_i o c_i = w
nodes.statement: Let S be a D-scheme (notation of 1.1, F of order q = p^r). The map G -> (I_{chi_i}, cbar_i : I_{chi_{i+1}} -> I_{chi_i}^{(x)p}, dbar_i : I_{chi_i}^{(x)p} -> I_{chi_{i+1}})_{i in Z/rZ} is a bijection. Its source is the set of isomorphism classes of S-schemes in F-vector spaces G satisfying (**). Its target is the set of isomorphism classes of systems of r invertible O_S-modules L_i with r pairs of O_S-linear maps cbar_i : L_{i+1} -> L_i^{(x)p} and dbar_i : L_i^{(x)p} -> L_{i+1} satisfying dbar_i o cbar_i = w id_{L_{i+1}} for all i, where w = p u is the universal constant of Proposition 1.3.1. Under this bijection the algebra of G is the O_S-module O_S (+) direct sum over chi in M of I_chi, with I_chi = prod_i L_i^{a_i} for chi = prod chi_i^{a_i} (0 <= a_i <= p-1, not all zero). Multiplication is the canonical isomorphism when a'_i + a''_i <= p-1 for all i (19), and the p-th power on generators is dbar_i (19 bis); comultiplication is the explicit formula (21) determined by the cbar_i. The Cartier dual corresponds to (L_i^vee, dbar_i^t, cbar_i^t) (Remark 1.5.3).
hypotheses: S a D-scheme (hypothesis (*))
G an S-scheme in F-vector spaces, finite flat of finite presentation, satisfying (**)
uses that w_chi is a unit (Proposition 1.3.1(1)), so c_chi and d_chi are isomorphisms
proofSteps: Forward map (18)-(19 bis): for chi = prod chi_i^{a_i}, compose c_chi and d_chi with the canonical isomorphisms of tensor powers; since d_chi o c_chi = w_chi is a unit, the I_chi are identified with monomials in the L_i. This gives the algebra structure (19), (19 bis).

Coalgebra (20)-(21): for chi' chi'' = chi_i there is a unique h in (0, r] with a'_{i-h} + a''_{i-h} = p, a'_{i-k} + a''_{i-k} = p-1 for 0 < k < h, and the other exponents zero. Computing the iterated comultiplication in two ways by associativity (6), and using that c_{chi'}, c_{chi''} are invertible, shows that c_{chi',chi''} is determined by the cbar_j via (21).

Inverse map: from (L_i, cbar_i, dbar_i) build the algebra A = O_S (+) direct sum of monomials with the multiplication (19)-(19 bis). A is generated by the I_chi, so it has at most one bialgebra structure whose comultiplication satisfies (21).

Existence is local on S, so reduce to S affine with free L_i and then to the universal case S = Spec(E), E = D[U_1..U_r, V_1..V_r]/(U_i V_i - w), with universal algebra A = E[X_1..X_r]/(X_i^p - v_i X_{i+1}).

E is a domain in which p is not a zero divisor, so the comultiplication identities may be checked after inverting p. They may also be checked after the finite free, faithfully flat extension E' = E[T]/(T^{q-1} - v_1^{p^{r-1}} v_2^{p^{r-2}} ... v_r).

Lemma 1.4.2: over S' = Spec(E') there is a morphism of F-vector space schemes H -> G_{S'}, H the constant scheme defined by F^+, which is an isomorphism after inverting p. Solve T_i^p = v_i T_{i+1} (23) with the image t_1 of T (24); the t_i are non-zero-divisors and are invertible after inverting p, because u_i v_i = w = p times a unit. Define alpha : A (x)_E E' -> B by X_i -> t_i epsilon_{chi_i}.

Check that (alpha (x) alpha) o c(X_i) and c_H o alpha(X_i) have the same component w^h t_i/(w_{chi'} w_{chi''}) along epsilon_{chi'} (x) epsilon_{chi''}, using (12), (20), (21) and (23). Since alpha is injective, c extends to a comultiplication on A compatible with the F-action.
acceptance: For r = 1 (F = F_p) the classification specializes to the Oort-Tate classification of group schemes of order p cited as [10].
Remark 1.5.3: the Cartier dual of the system (L_i, cbar_i, dbar_i) is (L_i^vee, dbar_i^t, cbar_i^t); check this on mu_p versus Z/pZ.
Check that when p is invertible on S every such G is etale (both cbar_i and dbar_i are isomorphisms since w is a unit), matching Proposition 1.2.2.

nodes.title: Over a local base, F-vector space schemes with (**) are given by pairs (gamma_i, delta_i) with gamma_i delta_i = w and equations X_i^p = delta_i X_{i+1}
nodes.statement: Let S = Spec(R) be a D-scheme with R local. An S-scheme in F-vector spaces satisfying (**) is equivalent to r pairs (gamma_i, delta_i) of elements of R with gamma_i delta_i = w for all i. G has the system of equations X_i^p = delta_i X_{i+1}, and its comultiplication is c(X_i) = X_i (x) 1 + 1 (x) X_i + sum over chi' chi'' = chi_i of (gamma_{i-h} ... gamma_{i-1})/(w_{chi'} w_{chi''}) (prod_j X_j^{a'_j}) (x) (prod_j X_j^{a''_j}), where chi' = prod chi_j^{a'_j}, chi'' = prod chi_j^{a''_j} and h is defined by (20). Two families (gamma_i, delta_i), (gamma'_i, delta'_i) define isomorphic F-vector space schemes if and only if there are units u_i of R with delta'_i = u_i^p delta_i u_{i+1}^{-1} and gamma_i = u_i^p gamma'_i u_{i+1}^{-1} for all i.
hypotheses: R local and a D-algebra (so every invertible O_S-module is free)
G satisfies (**)
proofSteps: Every invertible module over a local ring is free; choose generators of the L_i, so that cbar_i and dbar_i become multiplication by elements gamma_i and delta_i of R with gamma_i delta_i = w (Theorem 1.4.1).
The algebra relations (19 bis) become X_i^p = delta_i X_{i+1}, and the comultiplication formula (21) becomes the displayed formula.
A change of generators X_i -> u_i X_i changes (gamma_i, delta_i) by the displayed unit rule, and Theorem 1.4.1 says these are all isomorphisms.
acceptance: For r = 1, R = Z_p[mu_{p-1}]: (gamma, delta) = (w, 1) gives an etale group (X^p = X) and (1, w) gives X^p = w X, of multiplicative type; check against Z/pZ and mu_p.

nodes.title: Over a strictly henselian mixed-characteristic DVR, F-vector space schemes of rank q correspond to exponent families 0 <= n_i <= e
nodes.statement: Let R be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with fraction field of characteristic 0, residue characteristic p, normalized valuation v (v(pi) = 1) and absolute ramification index e = v(p), viewed as a D-algebra. There is a canonical bijection between isomorphism classes of R-schemes in F-vector spaces of rank q and families of r integers (n_i) with 0 <= n_i <= e for all i, given by n_i = v(delta_i) in the notation of Corollary 1.5.1.
hypotheses: R a strictly henselian DVR, fraction field of characteristic zero, residue characteristic p, e = v(p)
R is given a D-algebra structure (possible for a henselian local ring whose residue field contains F_q, Example (a) of 1.2)
condition (**) holds automatically by Proposition 1.2.2 (R integral with characteristic-zero fraction field)
proofSteps: By Corollary 1.5.1 a scheme G is given by pairs (gamma_i, delta_i) with gamma_i delta_i = w and v(w) = v(p) = e (Proposition 1.3.1(2)), so 0 <= v(delta_i) <= e; set n_i = v(delta_i).
Surjectivity: take delta_i = pi^{n_i} and gamma_i = w pi^{-n_i}.

Injectivity: if the families have the same valuations, they differ by units alpha_i: gamma'_i = alpha_i gamma_i, delta'_i = alpha_i^{-1} delta_i. One needs units u_i with delta'_i u_{i+1} = delta_i u_i^p for all i (Corollary 1.5.1); eliminating gives u_i^{q-1} = alpha_i^{p^{r-1}} alpha_{i+1}^{p^{r-2}} ... alpha_{i+r-1}, which has a solution because R is strictly henselian.
acceptance: For e = 1 the rank-q F-vector space schemes are indexed by {0,1}^r. Check that n_i = 0 for all i gives an etale scheme (stated in 3.3(c), p. 267). Check via the Cartier-dual system of Remark 1.5.3 that n_i = e for all i gives the Cartier dual of an etale scheme.

Remark 1.5.4 (stated with "on peut montrer", no proof): over a complete local base, (gamma_i, delta_i) is the kernel of p on a p-divisible group iff for every i one of gamma_i, delta_i is a unit; always true for an absolutely unramified mixed-characteristic DVR. Record this as an unproved remark, not as an input.

nodes.title: Schematic closure of a generic closed subgroup in a group scheme over a DVR, and finiteness of the quotient
nodes.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K, residue characteristic p, uniformizer pi and normalized valuation v; in mixed characteristic set e = v(p). Let X be an R-scheme of finite type with generic fibre X_K and Y a closed subscheme of X_K. The schematic closure of Y in X is the smallest closed subscheme Ybar of X containing Y. On an affine open U = Spec(A) with generic ideal I of A (x)_R K, Ybar is defined by the inverse image of I in A. Hence A/(ideal of Ybar) injects into (A (x) K)/I, so it is torsion free, and Ybar is flat over R with Ybar (x)_R K = Y. Formation of the closure commutes with fibre products over R. Consequently, if X is an R-group scheme and Y a closed subgroup scheme of X_K, then Ybar is a closed subgroup scheme of X, flat over R. If moreover X is finite over R, then Ybar is finite and the fppf quotient X/Ybar is representable by a scheme finite over R.
hypotheses: R a discrete valuation ring (any characteristics in 2.1), X of finite type over R
for the group statement: X an R-group scheme and Y a closed subgroup of the generic fibre
for the quotient statement: X finite over R
proofSteps: On each affine open, define the closure ideal as the inverse image of the generic ideal; the quotient ring embeds in the generic quotient and is therefore R-torsion free, so flat over R (Raynaud cites EGA IV_2 [5], p. 33, for flatness of torsion-free modules over a DVR).

Fibre products (Raynaud: "Il en resulte"; the following expansion is not written in the source): the closure of Y x_K Y' in X x_R X' is Ybar x_R Ybar'. The latter is flat with generic fibre Y x_K Y', and a flat closed subscheme is the closure of its generic fibre.
Group structure: the multiplication and inverse of X restricted to Ybar x Ybar land in the closure of Y, by the fibre product compatibility, so Ybar is a flat closed subgroup scheme.

Quotient: for X finite over R and Ybar finite flat, the fppf quotient X/Ybar is asserted representable by a finite R-scheme; Raynaud states this without proof or reference (the standard input is the quotient theorem for finite flat group schemes, e.g. SGA 3; not read here).
acceptance: Check on X = mu_{p,R} x (Z/pZ)_R over R = Z_p that the closure of the diagonal copy of the generic group is flat but that a closed subgroup of the special fibre not coming from the generic fibre is not a closure.
Check that the closure of a generic subgroup of a finite flat group need not be a direct factor, but is always finite flat.

nodes.title: Domination order on finite flat prolongations of a commutative K-group and existence of suprema and infima
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite commutative K-group scheme and let G1, G2 be finite flat R-group schemes (necessarily commutative) prolonging G, with generic fibres identified with G. G1 dominates G2 (G1 >= G2) if there is an R-morphism u : G1 -> G2 extending the identity of G. Such a u is unique and is a homomorphism. Identifying the rings A1, A2 of G1, G2 with subrings of the ring A of G, G1 >= G2 holds exactly when A2 is contained in A1. This defines a partial order on isomorphism classes of finite flat prolongations of G. Proposition 2.2.2: any two finite flat prolongations G1, G2 of G have a supremum and an infimum.
hypotheses: R a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K
G finite commutative over K; prolongations finite and flat over R
proofSteps: Uniqueness of u and the ring-inclusion criterion: a morphism of flat R-schemes is determined by its generic fibre, since the rings are R-torsion free and embed in A.

Supremum: in G1 x_R G2, with generic fibre G x_K G, take the kernel N of G x_K G -> G, (g, g') -> g - g', and its schematic closure Ncal (node schematic-closure-of-a-generic-subgroup-over-a-dvr). The two projections p1 o i, p2 o i induce the same isomorphism on generic fibres, so Ncal is a finite flat prolongation of G dominating G1 and G2; it is immediately a least upper bound.
Infimum: apply the supremum construction to the Cartier duals, since Cartier duality reverses the domination order.
acceptance: Over R = Z_p with G = mu_p (x) K: the prolongations mu_p and Z/pZ-type models (when they exist) are comparable; check that Cartier duality reverses the order.
Check that the supremum construction produces G1 when G1 >= G2.

nodes.title: Maximal (etale case) and minimal (multiplicative case) finite flat prolongations; both exist in characteristic zero
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite commutative K-group scheme admitting a finite flat prolongation over R. (1) If G is etale (resp. of multiplicative type), its set of finite flat prolongations has a maximum G+ (resp. a minimum G-). (2) If K has characteristic zero, the finite flat prolongations of G have both a maximum and a minimum.
hypotheses: R a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K
G finite commutative over K with at least one finite flat prolongation
for (2): char K = 0, so G is etale and its Cartier dual is etale
proofSteps: (2) is a special case of (1), since in characteristic zero G and its Cartier dual are both etale; the two halves of (1) are exchanged by Cartier duality.
For G etale with K-algebra A, the R-algebra of any finite flat prolongation is contained in the integral closure of R in A, which is finite over R.
Combining this with Proposition 2.2.2 (suprema) gives a maximum: an increasing chain of finite R-subalgebras of a finite R-module stabilizes.

For G = mu_p over Q_p: the minimum is mu_p over Z_p.

nodes.title: A p-divisible group over K whose levels all prolong to finite flat R-groups prolongs to a p-divisible group over R, uniquely
nodes.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic with residue characteristic p. Let G = (G_n)_{n >= 0} be a p-divisible group over K such that every G_n prolongs to a finite flat R-group scheme. Then G prolongs to a p-divisible group over R, unique up to isomorphism.
hypotheses: R a DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p)
G a p-divisible group over K in the sense of Tate [13]
uniqueness uses Tate's theorem ([13], p. 180): morphisms of generic fibres of p-divisible groups over R extend uniquely
proofSteps: Uniqueness: by Tate's full faithfulness on generic fibres ([13], p. 180), imported and not read here.

(a) Choose finite flat prolongations G(n) of G_n. By induction on n one may modify G(n+1) so that G_n -> G_{n+1} extends to G(n) -> G(n+1): dualize, take the schematic closure in G(n+1)' x G(n)' of the graph of the dual epimorphism G'_{n+1} -> G'_n, and dualize back.

(b) Filter G(n) by the closures G(n)_i of the G_i, i <= n. The successive quotients G(n)_i/G(n)_{i-1} =: Gamma_i^n prolong G_1, and the maps of (a) give Gamma_i^n -> Gamma_i^{n+1} (*), so for fixed i the Gamma_i^n decrease in the domination order.
(c) Multiplication by p induces Gamma_i^n -> Gamma_{i-1}^n (**), so for fixed n the Gamma_i^n increase with i.
(d) By Corollary 2.2.3 the decreasing sequence (*) is stationary with value Gamma^i. By (**) the Gamma^i increase, so they are stationary for i >= i_0, again by Corollary 2.2.3.

(e) Replace G(n) by G(n)/G(n)_{i_0}, so that one may take i_0 = 1. Then (**) is an isomorphism for large n, so by devissage the sequences 0 -> G(n)_i -> G(n)_{i+j} -> G(n)_{i+j}/G(n)_i -> 0 are exact for large n. The stationary values Gcal_i of G(n)_i -> G(n+1)_i -> ... then form exact sequences 0 -> Gcal_i -> Gcal_{i+j} -> Gcal_j -> 0, so (Gcal_i) is a p-divisible group over R prolonging G.
acceptance: Apply to G = mu_{p^infinity} over Q_p: the prolongation is mu_{p^infinity} over Z_p.
Check that step (d) genuinely needs Corollary 2.2.3 (a bounded monotone family of finite flat prolongations stabilizes), which uses char K = 0.

nodes.title: Tame inertia of a strictly henselian DVR as the inverse limit of mu_{q-1}(k), and the surjections j_q
nodes.statement: Let R be a strictly henselian DVR with residue field k of characteristic p, K a separable closure of K, so Gal(Kbar/K) is the inertia group I. There is a canonical exact sequence 0 -> I_p -> Gal(Kbar/K) -> I_t -> 0 with I_p the pro-p wild inertia and I_t the tame quotient of order prime to p. For n prime to p there is a unique subextension K_n of degree n, Galois, with a canonical isomorphism i_n : Gal(K_n/K) -> mu_n(K) characterized by x'^sigma = x' i_n(sigma)^{v'(x')} (1 + u') with v'(u') >= 1 for x' in K_n, v' the normalized valuation of K_n; these are compatible for m | n. Hence I_t is identified with the inverse limit of mu_n(K) over (n, p) = 1 and, via mu_n(K) = mu_n(k) and k_q^* = mu_{q-1}(k) for the subfields k_q with q = p^h elements, with the inverse limit of k_q^* under the norms x' -> x'^{(q'-1)/(q-1)}. j : I_t -> lim k_q^* denotes this identification and j_q : I_t -> mu_{q-1}(k) -> mu_{q-1}(K) the canonical surjection.
hypotheses: R strictly henselian discrete valuation ring, residue characteristic p
the description of the tame quotient is quoted from Serre [12], Section 1
proofSteps: Raynaud states that the whole of 3.1 is taken directly from Serre, Proprietes galoisiennes des points d'ordre fini des courbes elliptiques [12], Section 1; the existence and uniqueness of K_n, the canonical isomorphism i_n and its compatibilities are recalled, not proved.
Pass from the mu_n(K)-description to the k_q^* description using mu_n(K) = mu_n(k) for (n, p) = 1 and the norm maps as transition maps.
acceptance: Check that the norm k_{q'}^* -> k_q^* for q' = q^r is x -> x^{(q'-1)/(q-1)}.

Check the normalization: sigma(x') = x' (i_n(sigma))^{v'(x')} (1 + u') with v'(u') >= 1 (read on the page image of p. 263). So for a uniformizer pi_n of K_n with pi_n^n = pi, sigma(pi_n)/pi_n is an n-th root of unity congruent to i_n(sigma), hence equal to it. This fixes the convention for the tame characters consumed by R07.5 and by Serre-weight recipes.

nodes.title: Jordan-Hoelder quotients of etale or multiplicative p-power groups over a strictly henselian base are F-vector space schemes with (**)
nodes.statement: Let R be strictly henselian and G a finite commutative K-group scheme killed by a power of p that is etale or of multiplicative type. For each successive quotient G_i of a Jordan-Hoelder series of G there is a finite field F_i of characteristic p such that G_i is a K-scheme in F_i-vector spaces satisfying (**).
hypotheses: R strictly henselian (henselian suffices for the tame-ramification step)
G finite commutative over K, killed by a power of p, etale or of multiplicative type
proofSteps: By devissage each Jordan-Hoelder quotient G_i is killed by p.
Etale case, R henselian: a finite commutative etale K-group killed by p is an F_p-vector space V with a linear Galois action rho, and conversely.

If G_i is simple, rho is simple. The wild inertia I_p is a normal pro-p subgroup, and a pro-p group acting on a nonzero F_p-vector space has nonzero invariants (Serre, Corps locaux [11], p. 146). The invariants V^{I_p} are rho-stable, so by simplicity I_p acts trivially and rho is tamely ramified.

With R strictly henselian, rho factors through the commutative group I_t. Let F be the commutant of rho in Aut(V), a finite field; rho(I_t) consists of F-homotheties, and by simplicity V has F-dimension 1.
Hence G_i is a K-scheme in F-vector spaces satisfying (**) (Proposition 1.2.2). The multiplicative case follows by Cartier duality.
acceptance: For G = E[p] of an elliptic curve with good supersingular reduction over an unramified strictly henselian base, G is simple and F has p^2 elements (Raynaud's Example after 3.4.7).
Check that without strict henselianity the commutant argument fails because Gal(Kbar/K) need not be abelian modulo wild inertia.

nodes.title: The F-vector space structure of the generic fibre extends to the maximal and minimal prolongations
nodes.statement: Let R have mixed characteristic and let Gcal be a finite flat R-group scheme whose generic fibre G is a K-scheme in F-vector spaces. Then the F-vector space scheme structure of G extends to the maximal prolongation G+ and to the minimal prolongation G- of G.
hypotheses: R a DVR of mixed characteristic (so Corollary 2.2.3(2) applies)
G has at least one finite flat prolongation
proofSteps: In characteristic zero G+ and G- exist (Corollary 2.2.3).

Every automorphism of G extends to G+ and to G-, which Raynaud calls formal: for an automorphism a of G, (id, a) transports prolongations to prolongations and preserves the order, so it preserves the maximum and minimum.
In particular the homotheties by elements of F extend, giving the F-vector space structure on G+ and G-.

nodes.title: Comparison of two F-vector space prolongations through the valuations of the transition units alpha_i
nodes.statement: Let R have mixed characteristic and let Gcal and Gcal' be R-schemes in F-vector spaces of rank q = p^r with the same generic fibre G. By Corollary 1.5.1 they have equations X_i^p = delta_i X_{i+1} (1) and X'_i^p = delta'_i X'_{i+1} (1'), with 0 <= v(delta_i), v(delta'_i) <= e (2), (2'). The generic isomorphism is X'_i = alpha_i X_i with alpha_i in K^* (3), so delta'_i = alpha_i^p delta_i alpha_{i+1}^{-1} (4), and Gcal >= Gcal' iff v(alpha_i) >= 0 for all i (5). Suppose Gcal >= Gcal'. (a) If some alpha_j is not a unit (Gcal > Gcal'), taking i with v(alpha_i) >= 1 maximal gives v(delta'_i) >= p-1, hence e >= p-1. (b) If the alpha_j do not all have the same valuation, some i has v(alpha_i) > v(alpha_{i+1}), so v(delta'_i) >= p and e >= p. Conversely, if v(delta_i) >= p one may take alpha_i = pi and alpha_j = 1 for j != i, obtaining Gcal > Gcal' with sum_j v(delta'_j) > sum_j v(delta_j). (c) If all alpha_j have the same positive valuation and v(delta'_j) <= p-1 for all j, then v(alpha_j) = 1, v(delta_j) = 0 and v(delta'_j) = p-1 for all j. Then Gcal is etale, and if e = p-1 then Gcal' is of multiplicative type.
hypotheses: R a DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p), e = v(p)
both prolongations are R-schemes in F-vector spaces of rank q (so Corollary 1.5.1 applies after the D-structure of R is fixed)
proofSteps: Write both prolongations by Corollary 1.5.1 and compare generic coordinates; (4) is the transformation rule of Corollary 1.5.1 with alpha_i in K^* instead of units.
Criterion (5): Gcal >= Gcal' means the generic identity maps the ring of Gcal' into that of Gcal, i.e. X'_i = alpha_i X_i are integral.
Cases (a), (b), (c) are direct valuation estimates on (4) against the bounds (2').
acceptance: Numerical check at r = 1: delta' = alpha^{p-1} delta, so a strict domination forces v(delta') >= p-1 and hence e >= p-1.
Check that case (b) cannot occur when r = 1.

nodes.title: Characterization of the maximal prolongation of an F-vector space scheme on equations of type (1)
nodes.statement: Let G be a K-scheme in F-vector spaces of rank q admitting a finite flat prolongation over R (R of mixed characteristic). The maximal prolongation G+ of G is characterized, on equations of type (1), by: (a) v(delta_i) <= p-1 for all i; (b) there exists i with v(delta_i) < p-1.
hypotheses: R a DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p)
G a K-scheme in F-vector spaces of rank q with a finite flat prolongation
proofSteps: By Proposition 3.3.1, G+ is an F-vector space scheme, so it has equations of type (1).

nodes.title: If e < p-1, a finite flat prolongation of an F-vector space scheme is unique and is an F-vector space scheme
nodes.statement: Let R have mixed characteristic (0, p) with e < p-1, and let G be a K-scheme in F-vector spaces of rank q admitting a finite flat prolongation Gcal. Then Gcal is, up to isomorphism, the unique finite flat prolongation of G over R, and it is an R-scheme in F-vector spaces.
hypotheses: R a DVR of mixed characteristic with absolute ramification index e < p-1 (in particular p >= 3)
G a K-scheme in F-vector spaces of rank q with some finite flat prolongation
proofSteps: Apply case (a) of the valuation analysis with Gcal = G+ and Gcal' = G-, which are F-vector space schemes by Proposition 3.3.1. Since e < p-1, strict domination is impossible, so G+ = G-.
Every finite flat prolongation lies between G- and G+ in the domination order (Corollary 2.2.3), hence equals both, and carries the F-structure of G+.
acceptance: The hypothesis cannot be relaxed to e <= p-1: for e = p-1 the etale and multiplicative prolongations can differ (Proposition 3.3.2(3)).
At p = 2 every mixed-characteristic DVR has e >= 1 = p-1, so this uniqueness never applies at p = 2; any dyadic uniqueness must come from a separate theorem.

nodes.title: For e = p-1, a simple F-vector space scheme has either a unique prolongation or exactly an etale and a multiplicative one
nodes.statement: Let R be a henselian DVR of mixed characteristic with e = p-1, and let G be a simple K-scheme in F-vector spaces of rank q admitting a finite flat prolongation Gcal. Then either Gcal is the unique prolongation of G, or G has exactly two prolongations, one etale and one of multiplicative type. In all cases these prolongations are R-schemes in F-vector spaces.
hypotheses: R henselian, mixed characteristic, e = p-1
G simple, with a finite flat prolongation
proofSteps: Consider G+ and G-, which are F-vector space schemes, and suppose G+ != G-. By cases (a), (b), (c) of the valuation analysis, G+ is etale and G- is of multiplicative type.
Show that any prolongation Gcal equals G+ or G-. Since G+ is etale, R henselian and G simple, Gcal (x)_R k is simple, so if the canonical u : G+ -> G- is not an isomorphism then u (x)_R k = 0.

Show that Gcal is of multiplicative type when u (x) k = 0: one may assume S strictly henselian and, by devissage, G of rank p; then Gcal is an F_p-vector space scheme which is not etale, hence of multiplicative type (Corollary 1.5.2 with r = 1).

For F-vector space schemes, u is an isomorphism by Proposition 3.3.2(2).

nodes.title: Raynaud Corollary 3.3.6(1): for e < p-1 every generic morphism of finite flat p-power groups extends uniquely
nodes.statement: Let R be a DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p) with e < p-1, and let Gcal, Hcal be finite flat commutative R-group schemes killed by a power of p, with generic fibres G, H. Every morphism G -> H extends uniquely to an R-morphism u : Gcal -> Hcal. In other words, the generic-fibre functor is fully faithful on these objects.
hypotheses: R a DVR of mixed characteristic, e < p-1
Gcal, Hcal commutative, finite and flat over R, killed by a power of p
proofSteps: Source status: Raynaud states Corollary 3.3.6 immediately after Theorem 3.3.3 and Remarks 3.3.4-3.3.5 and gives no written proof.
Uniqueness of an extension needs no ramification hypothesis: Gcal is flat, so a morphism is determined by its generic fibre (the ring-inclusion argument of Definition 2.2.1).

Existence route not written in Raynaud: the schematic closure Gamma of the graph of f : G -> H in Gcal x_R Hcal is a finite flat prolongation of G (node schematic-closure-of-a-generic-subgroup-over-a-dvr). The first projection Gamma -> Gcal is the identity on generic fibres, so by Theorem 3.3.3 (via Proposition 2.2.2) it is an isomorphism, and u = pr_2 o pr_1^{-1}.

Written argument in Conrad (Corollary 1.6, stated for e = 1, p > 2, and extended to e < p-1 in Lemma 4.1): let Kcal be the schematic closure in Gcal of ker(f_K); replace Gcal by Gcal/Kcal so that f_K is a closed immersion; by Cartier duality f_K is then an isomorphism. A morphism of finite flat p-power groups is an isomorphism iff it is so on generic fibres (Conrad Corollary 1.5; for e < p-1 this is Raynaud Corollary 3.3.6 again), and Raynaud Proposition 2.2.2 then produces the extension. Conrad Lemma 4.1 proves the generic-fibre functor fully faithful and exact for e < p-1 and on unipotent objects for e <= p-1 by citing Raynaud Cor. 3.3.6(1), Prop. 3.3.2(3) and Thm 3.3.3.
acceptance: Two nonisomorphic integral models with the same generic fibre (mu_2 and Z/2Z over Z_2) show that full faithfulness fails when e = p-1 on all objects (Conrad p. 8: "It is because the group schemes mu_2 and Z/2 over Z_2 have isomorphic generic fibers that we need a restriction for p = 2"). It survives on unipotent or connected objects (Conrad Lemma 4.1).
Check the unwritten route against a written proof before any consumer imports existence of extensions.

nodes.title: Raynaud Theorem 3.4.1: Galois acts on a rank-q F-vector space scheme by the tame character psi = prod psi_{i+j}^{v(delta_{i+j-1})}
nodes.statement: Let R be strictly henselian of mixed characteristic, and let G be a K-scheme in F-vector spaces of rank q with equations (1) X_i^p = delta_i X_{i+1}, delta_i in K^*. Then Gal(Kbar/K) acts on the F-vector space G(Kbar) by homotheties through the character I_t -> mu_{q-1}(K) -> F^*, given by j_q followed by psi = psi_{i+1}^{v(delta_i)} ... psi_{i+r}^{v(delta_{i+r-1})}. Here psi_i : mu_{q-1}(K) -> F^* is the inverse of the fundamental character chi_i, so psi_i^p = psi_{i-1}. Remark 3.4.2: the representation is simple iff the composites of psi with the automorphisms of F are distinct, i.e. iff the sequence v(delta_j) is not invariant under a nontrivial power of the cyclic shift j -> j+1.
hypotheses: R strictly henselian DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p)
G a K-scheme in F-vector spaces with equations (1) (Corollary 1.5.1 over K)
proofSteps: Eliminating X_j for j != i, the points of G in Kbar are the solutions of X_i^q = a_i X_i (6) with a_i = delta_i^{p^{r-1}} delta_{i+1}^{p^{r-2}} ... delta_{i+r-1}.
G is trivialized by the tame extension L of degree q-1, and I_t acts on the one-dimensional F-vector space G(L) through a character I_t -> mu_{q-1}(K) -> F_q^* (7).
The coordinate X_i is attached to the fundamental character chi_i, so lambda x = chi_i(lambda) x for x in G(L), lambda in F (8).

With v' the normalized valuation of L, the nonzero roots of (6) have valuation v'(a_i)/(q-1) = v(a_i) = p^{r-1} v(delta_i) + ... + v(delta_{i+r-1}). By the tame inertia description of 3.1, sigma(x) = j_q(sigma)^{v(a_i)} x for sigma in I_t (9).
Hence sigma acts on G(L) as the homothety psi_i(j_q(sigma))^{v(a_i)}, and psi_i^{v(a_i)} = psi_{i+1}^{v(delta_i)} ... psi_{i+r}^{v(delta_{i+r-1})} using psi_i^p = psi_{i-1}.
acceptance: r = 1, G = mu_p over an unramified base (delta = p up to unit, v(delta) = 1): psi is the level-one fundamental character, i.e. the mod p cyclotomic character on inertia.
Check the direction of the index shift: psi_{i+1}^{v(delta_i)} (not psi_i^{v(delta_i)}), as printed on p. 270 and derived on p. 269.

nodes.title: Raynaud Theorem 3.4.3: an F-vector space scheme with character psi prolongs iff psi = prod psi_{i+j}^{n_j} with 0 <= n_j <= e
nodes.statement: Let R be strictly henselian of mixed characteristic, with absolute ramification index e, and let G be a K-scheme in F-vector spaces associated with a character psi : mu_{q-1}(K) -> F^*. G prolongs to a finite flat R-group scheme if and only if psi can be written as psi = psi_{i+1}^{n_1} ... psi_{i+r}^{n_r} with 0 <= n_j <= e for all j. Remark 3.4.6: if e >= p-1 every K-scheme in F-vector spaces prolongs to a finite R-group scheme, so Theorem 3.4.1 and Corollary 3.4.4 give no information in that range.
hypotheses: R strictly henselian DVR of mixed characteristic, absolute ramification index e
G a K-scheme in F-vector spaces of rank q (one-dimensional over F)
proofSteps: If G has a finite flat prolongation Gcal, one may assume the F-structure extends to Gcal (Proposition 3.3.2, via the maximal prolongation of Proposition 3.3.1).
Then Gcal has equations of type (1) whose only constraints are 0 <= v(delta_i) <= e (Corollaries 1.5.1-1.5.2), and Theorem 3.4.1 gives psi with exponents n_j = v(delta) in [0, e].
Conversely, for exponents in [0, e], Corollary 1.5.2 gives an R-scheme in F-vector spaces with v(delta_i) = n, whose generic fibre has character psi by Theorem 3.4.1.
Remark 3.4.6: for e >= p-1 every character psi has a p-adic writing with exponents in [0, p-1] (Section 1.1, formula (1)), all <= e, so every G prolongs.
acceptance: p = 2: every mixed-characteristic DVR has e >= 1 = p-1, so every F-vector space scheme prolongs and the criterion is vacuous; dyadic applications cannot use it as a constraint.
Unramified R, p odd: psi prolongs iff its exponents in fundamental characters are 0 or 1 (Serre's level-r fundamental-character condition used in Serre-weight recipes).

nodes.title: Invariant measures, Haar measures and the absolute different of a finite locally free commutative group; D(G) D(G') = (rank)
nodes.statement: Let S = Spec(R) be affine and G a finite commutative locally free S-group scheme of rank n, with bialgebra A, Cartier dual G' with bialgebra A', and pairing < , >. View A as functions and A' as measures, with convolution *. The invariant measures on G (mu with mu * f = <f, mu> 1 for all f, Lemma 2) form an invertible R-module D, a direct summand of A'. A Haar measure is a basis of D (Definition 5), i.e. an invariant measure that is nonzero on every fibre, and a Haar measure mu is a basis of the A-module A' (Lemma 6). The pairing restricted to D x D' is nondegenerate, where D' is the line of invariant measures on G' (Lemma 7). The trace theta of the R-algebra A is an invariant measure, theta = lambda mu, and the different of the R-algebra A is an ideal invariant under translations, hence comes from an ideal D(G) of R, the absolute different of G (Definition 8), with D(G) = lambda R. Proposition 9: D(G) D(G') is the ideal of R generated by the rank n.
hypotheses: S = Spec(R) affine; G finite, commutative, locally free of rank n over S
for Definition 8 and Proposition 9: R a ring over which the duality theory for finite locally complete intersection algebras applies (Tate [13], p. 165)
proofSteps: Lemma 1 and Lemma 2: characterize invariant measures by the commutative diagrams for the universal translation and by mu * f = <f, mu> 1 or mu * nu = <1, nu> mu.

Proposition 3 (proof communicated by A. Douady): with theta the trace of A in A' and T the trace of A' in A, <T, theta> = n, because theta is invariant, so the trace of mu -> theta * mu is the trace of mu -> <1, mu> theta, which is <1, theta> = n.

Lemma 4: the elements f with c(f) = 1 (x) f are exactly the constants lambda 1. Since G' is locally a complete intersection (as a subgroup of a smooth group), duality for coherent sheaves (Hartshorne, Residues and Duality [7], III Sections 6-7) makes A = Hom(A', R) locally isomorphic to A' as an A'-module; with Lemma 4 this shows that the invariant measures form an invertible direct summand D.
Lemma 5 (over a field: the smallest translation-stable subspace containing f is {nu * f}) and Lemma 6 (a Haar measure is an A-basis of A') and Lemma 7 (nondegeneracy on D x D').

Application: theta = lambda mu, and by duality for finite locally complete intersection algebras (Tate [13], p. 165) the different is lambda A, so D(G) = lambda R. Intrinsically D(G) is the image of v : D^{(x)-1} -> R dual to u : R -> D, 1 -> theta. Lemma 7 and Proposition 3 give Proposition 9.

For an R-scheme in F-vector spaces with equations (1) of 3.3 the relative different is generated by prod_i delta_i (used in Section 4.1).

nodes.title: Raynaud Theorem 4.1.1: for e <= p-1 the Galois action on det of the generic fibre of a finite flat group killed by p is tau_p^{v(D)}
nodes.statement: Let R be a strictly henselian DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p) with e <= p-1. Let Gcal be a finite, flat, commutative R-group scheme killed by p, of rank p^h, with generic fibre G (etale). Then the action of Gal(Kbar/K) on the etale group det(G) = Lambda^h G of rank p is given by the tame character tau_p^{v(D(Gcal))}. Here tau_p : I_t -> mu_{p-1}(K) -> F_p^* is j_p followed by the canonical isomorphism, and D(Gcal) is the absolute different of Gcal (Appendix, Definition 8).
hypotheses: R strictly henselian discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p)

From the equations (1), the relative different of Gcal over R is generated by prod_i delta_i, and so is the absolute different D(Gcal). Hence det(G) is given by tau_p^{v(D(Gcal))}.

nodes.title: Fontaine-Laffaille coefficient setup and the category MF of (A, tau, pi)-filtered Dieudonne modules
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, K_0 = Frac W(k), and e = [K : K_0]. Let E be a finite extension of Q_p contained in Kbar, with ring of integers O, uniformizer pi and residue field of q = p^r elements. Let E_0 = Frac W(F_q), and assume the canonical map E (x)_{E_0} K_0 -> K is an isomorphism, i.e. K = E K_0, e = [E : E_0], and pi is also a uniformizer of the ring of integers A of K. Let tau be the continuous E_0-automorphism of K = E (x)_{E_0} K_0 given by tau(x (x) a) = x (x) sigma^r(a), so that K^tau = E, A^tau = O and tau acts on k by x -> x^q. An (A, tau, pi)-filtered Dieudonne module is an A-module M with a decreasing, exhaustive, separated filtration (M^i)_{i in Z} by A-submodules and tau-semilinear maps phi^i_M : M^i -> M with phi^{i+1}_M(x) = pi phi^i_M(x) for x in M^{i+1}. Morphisms are A-linear maps compatible with the filtrations and the phi^i. The resulting category MF is additive and O-linear. Equivalently (1.4(b)), an object is a filtered module together with an A-linear map phi_M : Mtilde -> M_tau, where Mtilde is the inductive limit of the diagram M^{i+1} -> M^i (inclusion) and M^{i+1} -> M^i (multiplication by pi). MF_tor is the full subcategory of objects of finite A-length with sum_i Im phi^i_M = M. For E = Q_p (so q = p, pi = p, tau = sigma, O = Z_p), this forces e = 1, i.e. K = K_0.
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field; E finite over Q_p inside Kbar, containing a uniformizer of K, with K = E (x)_{E_0} K_0
q = #(O/pi) = p^r; tau acts on k as the q-th power map
proofSteps: 0.3: impose K = E K_0 so that tau is defined, and record K^tau = E, A^tau = O.
1.1-1.3: define the tau-twist M_tau and the category MF with its O-linear structure.
1.4(b): rewrite the compatibility phi^{i+1} = pi phi^i as a single map phi_M : Mtilde -> M_tau on the inductive limit.
1.5: define MF_tor by finite length and the surjectivity condition sum Im phi^i_M = M.
acceptance: For E = Q_p check that the setup is exactly an absolutely unramified K = K_0 with Z_p-coefficients.

For K ramified (e > 1) the theory applies only after choosing E with e = [E : E_0] containing a uniformizer of K, with coefficients in O and filtration bound q rather than p. Check this against the atlas text of R07.3, which restricts to e = 1.
1.4(a): changing pi to u pi for a unit u of O gives an isomorphic category.

nodes.title: MF_tor is abelian and artinian, with kernels, cokernels and subobject filtrations computed in MF
nodes.statement: Let M be a filtered module whose underlying A-module has finite length. Proposition 1.6: M is in MF_tor iff phi_M : Mtilde -> M_tau is surjective, iff it is injective, iff it is bijective. Lemma 1.7: lg_A Mtilde = lg_A M. Lemma 1.9: if (L, (L^i)) is a filtered submodule of a finite-length (M, (M^i)) with Ltilde -> Mtilde injective, then L^i = M^i intersect L for all i. Proposition 1.8: MF_tor is abelian and artinian, and the kernel (resp. cokernel) of a morphism of MF_tor is also a kernel (resp. cokernel) in MF. Explicitly, a kernel carries the induced filtration, an image carries the filtration L^i = image of M'^i, which coincides with L intersect M^i, and a cokernel carries the image (quotient) filtration. Section 1.11: MF embeds fully faithfully in an abelian O-linear category MFcal whose objects are families (M, M^i, alpha^i, beta^i, phi^i). Kernels and cokernels of morphisms of MF_tor computed in MFcal agree with those in MF_tor, and an extension in MFcal of objects of MF (resp. MF_tor) is again in MF (resp. MF_tor).
hypotheses: objects of MF_tor: finite A-length and sum Im phi^i = M
proofSteps: Lemma 1.7: with M^j = M and M^{f+1} = 0, the exact sequence 0 -> direct sum_{i=j+1}^{f} M^i -> direct sum_{i=j}^{f} M^i -> Mtilde -> 0 (4) gives lg Mtilde = lg M^j = lg M.
Proposition 1.6: (i) <=> (ii) is the definition; since lg Mtilde = lg M_tau, surjectivity, injectivity and bijectivity of phi_M are equivalent.

Lemma 1.9: if y is in M^i intersect L but not in L^i, choose s < i with y in L^s minus L^{s+1} and pi y in L^{s+1}. The element z with components y at s and -pi y at s+1 has nonzero image in Ltilde but zero image in Mtilde, contradicting injectivity.

Proof of 1.8 (1.10): (a) the kernel N' with induced filtration and restricted phi is a kernel in MF; a length count via Lemma 1.7 shows 0 -> Ntilde' -> Mtilde' -> Ltilde -> 0 exact, so phi_{N'} is injective and N' is in MF_tor by 1.6.

(b) The image L receives a unique isomorphism phi_L making the diagram commute, so L is a coimage. Injectivity of Ltilde -> Mtilde and Lemma 1.9 give L^i = L intersect M^i. The cokernel with image filtration is in MF_tor because phi_N is surjective.
(c) Image equals coimage, so MF_tor is abelian; (d) artinian because objects have finite length.
acceptance: Check on the reduction of a lattice object modulo pi^n (7.14) that the quotient filtration is the image filtration, as required when torsion subquotients change the filtration.
Check that MF itself is not abelian (1.11) but MF_tor is.

nodes.statement: MF_tor^{f,q} is the full subcategory of MF_tor consisting of objects with M^0 = M and M^q = 0, i.e. filtration jumps in [0, q-1]. nodes.title: The filtered Galois ring S = W_A(R)[pi^{-1} xi_0^q] with its filtration and divided Frobenii phi^i_S
nodes.statement: Let C be the completion of Kbar and A_C its ring of integers. R = lim_{x -> x^p} Abar/pAbar, identified with sequences (x^{(m)}) in A_C with (x^{(m+1)})^p = x^{(m)}; v_R(x) = v(x^{(0)}) with v(p) = 1 is a complete valuation, and R is perfect with residue field k. W_A(R) = A (x)_{W(k)} W(R) and W_K(R) = K (x)_{W(k)} W(R); every element of W_A(R) is uniquely sum pi^n [u_n] (2.3). The map theta^0 : W_K(R) -> C, sum pi^n [u_n] -> sum pi^n u_n^{(0)}, is a K-algebra homomorphism ([F2], Prop. 2.4) whose kernel W^1_K(R) is principal, generated by xi_0 = [x_0] + pi for x_0 in R with x_0^{(0)} = -pi. Phi(sum pi^n [u_n]) = sum pi^n [u_n^q] is a tau-semilinear ring automorphism. W_K(R) is a filtered module with W^i_K(R) = W_K(R) for i <= 0, the i-th power of W^1_K(R) for i >= 1, and phi^i = pi^{-i} Phi (2.6). S is the set of sum pi^n [u_n] with v_R(u_{-m}) >= m q v(pi) = m q/e for all m > 0; it is the subring W_A(R)[pi^{-1}[x]] for any x with v_R(x) = q/e. S is a filtered module with S^i = W^i_K(R) intersect {x in S : Phi x in pi^i S} and phi^i_S = restriction of phi^i, compatible with multiplication (S^i S^j in S^{i+j}, phi^{i+j}(xy) = phi^i(x) phi^j(y)). G = Gal(Kbar/K) acts on S commuting with Phi and the filtration, making S an O[G]-module in MF (3.1). Lemma 5.4: S = W_A(R)[pi^{-1} xi_0^q]; for 0 <= i < q, S^i = W^i_K(R) intersect S is the ideal generated by xi_0^i and pi^{-1} xi_0^q; with eta = pi^{-1}[x_0^q] + 1 one has phi^i_S(xi_0^i) = eta^i and phi^i_S(pi^{-1} xi_0^q) = pi^{q-1-i} eta^q.
hypotheses: setup of 0.3 (E, O, pi, q, tau, K = E K_0)
imports: the tilt R and its valuation ([F4] Ch. V Section 1, [F-W]); theta^0 and its kernel ([F2], Prop. 2.4)

2.5: theta^0 is a homomorphism with principal kernel generated by xi_0 ([F2], Prop. 2.4); Phi is tau-semilinear.
2.6-2.7: define the filtration and phi^i on W_K(R), then S and its filtration; check that S is a subring containing W_A(R) and pi^{-1}[x].

5.4 proof: pi^{-1} xi_0^q - pi^{-1}[x_0^q] lies in pi W_A(R), so eta is in S and S = W_A(R)[pi^{-1} xi_0^q]. For 1 <= i < q, W_A(R) intersect W^i_K(R) = xi_0^i W_A(R), which gives the generators of S^i. Phi(xi_0) = [x_0^q] + pi = pi eta then gives phi^i(xi_0^i) = eta^i and phi^i(pi^{-1} xi_0^q) = pi^{q-i-1} eta^q in S, since i < q.

Record that for E = Q_p, 8.4's proof identifies the completed S_K with Fontaine's ring B^+_a of [F2] Section 4 (not re-proved here).

Pour 0 <= i < q, on a S^i = W^i_K(R) intersect S et S^i est l'ideal de S engendre par xi_0^i et pi^{-1} xi_0^q; si eta = pi^{-1}[x_0^q] + 1, on a phi^i_S(xi_0^i) = eta^i et phi^i_S(pi^{-1} xi_0^q) = pi^{q-1-i} eta^q.

nodes.title: The contravariant functor U_S(M) = Ext^1_{MFcal}(M, S), identified with Hom(M, S_infinity)
nodes.statement: For M in MF (or in MFcal) the O[G]-action on S makes Ext^i_{MFcal}(M, S) a left O[G]-module, contravariant and O-linear in M, and U_S(M) := Ext^1(M, S). With S_n the cokernel of pi^n on S in MFcal (S_1 = Sbar) and transition maps pi_{S,n}, set S_infinity = lim S_n and S_E = lim(S -pi-> S -pi-> ...), which is W_K(R) as an object of MF; this gives the exact sequence 0 -> S -> S_E -> S_infinity -> 0 (1'). Lemma 3.8: for every M in MF_tor and every i >= 0, Ext^i_{MFcal}(M, S_infinity) is canonically and functorially Ext^{i+1}_{MFcal}(M, S); in particular U_S(M) = Hom_{MFcal}(M, S_infinity). Proposition 5.5: for M in MF_tor^{f,q}, U_S(M) = Hom_MF(M, T_infinity), where T_infinity is S_infinity with filtration truncated at q; for M killed by pi, U_S(M) = Hom_{MFtilde}(M, Ttilde) and Ext^1(M, Sbar) = Ext^1(M, Ttilde), with Ttilde the reduction of S modulo pi.
hypotheses: M in MF_tor (pi-power torsion) for Lemma 3.8; M in MF_tor^{f,q} for Proposition 5.5
proofSteps: Apply Ext^*(M, -) to (1'). Ext^i(M, S_E) is killed by a power of pi because M is pi-power torsion, while pi acts invertibly on it through S_E; hence it vanishes and the connecting map is an isomorphism (Lemma 3.8).
5.5: since S^i = W^i_K(R) intersect S for i < q, the maps alpha, beta of S_infinity (resp. Sbar) are injective in degrees < q, and for M with M^q = 0 only these degrees matter.
acceptance: The functor is contravariant: record this before comparing with covariant conventions (V_B versus its dual V_B^*, Theorem 8.4(ii)).
For E = Q_p and M = M(1; i), check U_S(M) against the character computed in Theorem 5.3(iii).

nodes.title: Simple objects of MF_tor over an algebraically closed residue field are the M(h; i) with i of exact period h
nodes.statement: Assume k algebraically closed. Let Mtilde be the full subcategory of MF_tor of objects killed by pi; an object is a finite-dimensional k-vector space with a filtration and a bijective tau-semilinear map phi_M : gr M -> M. For h >= 1 and i : Z/hZ -> Z, M(h; i) is k^{Z/hZ} with basis (e_m), filtration M^j = direct sum over i_m >= j of k e_m, and phi^{i_m}(e_m) = e_{m-1}. For a in F_{q^h}, v_a(e_m) = a^{q^{-m}} e_m gives an embedding F_{q^h} -> End(M(h; i)). The period of i is the least m >= 1 with i_{n+m} = i_n for all n. Proposition 4.4: (i) M(h; i) is simple iff i has period h, and then v is an isomorphism from F_{q^h} to End(M(h; i)); (ii) every simple object M of Mtilde has End(M) a finite extension of F_q of some degree h, and for each choice of isomorphism End(M) = F_{q^h} there is a unique i : Z/hZ -> Z of period h such that M is isomorphic to M(h; i) as an F_{q^h}-object. Remark 4.11: if i has period h' then M(h; i) is isotypic, a direct sum of h/h' copies of M(h'; i').
hypotheses: k algebraically closed
objects killed by pi (the simple objects of MF_tor are of this kind)
proofSteps: 4.6-4.7: with d^0(x) the filtration degree and f(x) = phi^{d^0(x)}(xbar), a subspace N is a subobject iff f(N) is contained in N.

Lemma 4.8: for M nonzero of dimension mu there are h with 1 <= h <= mu and x != 0 with f^h(x) = x. Take a minimal linear relation sum a_j f^j(x) = 0; minimality forces d^0 f^s(x) to be periodic; the span N of the f^n(x) meets the higher filtration trivially; f^h|_N is bijective and tau^h-semilinear; over algebraically closed k it has a fixed vector (Jacobson, The Theory of Rings [J1], Th. 15).
Lemma 4.9: Hom(M(h'; i'), M(h; i)) != 0 iff some shift m has i_{n+m} = i'_n for all n; and for period exactly h, End(M(h; i)) = F_{q^h} via v.

4.10: for simple M, map M(h; i_0, ..., i_{h-1}) -> M by e_{-n} -> f^n(x) with i_n = d^0 f^{h-n}(x); simplicity and dimension count make it an isomorphism. Simplicity of M(h; i) is then decided by Lemma 4.9 through the period of i.
acceptance: M(1; j) is the rank-one object with filtration jump j; for q = p these are the objects whose Galois modules are omega^j on inertia (Theorem 5.3(iii)).
Check the F_{q^h}-structure convention v_a(e_m) = a^{q^{-m}} e_m, which fixes the exponent in Theorem 5.3(iii).

nodes.title: Fontaine-Laffaille fundamental character of level h, chi_h : G -> F_{q^h}^*
nodes.statement: Assume k algebraically closed. For n prime to p, mu_n(Kbar) is cyclic of order n and reduces isomorphically onto mu_n(k). For a uniformizer pi' of K (e.g. pi' = pi) and a root pi_n of X^n = pi' in Kbar, K(pi_n) is the unique extension of K of degree n in Kbar, and eta_n : G -> Kbar^* defined by g(pi_n) = eta_n(g) pi_n is a homomorphism onto mu_n(Kbar) independent of the choices. For n = q^h - 1, mu_n(k) = F_{q^h}^*, and the fundamental character of level h is chi_h : G -> F_{q^h}^*, the composite of eta_{q^h-1} with the canonical isomorphism mu_{q^h-1}(Kbar) -> F_{q^h}^*.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed (so G is the inertia group)
q = #(O/pi), with pi a uniformizer of K by the setup of 0.3
proofSteps: Kummer theory for tame extensions over a strictly henselian base (stated in 5.1 without proof).
acceptance: Compare with Raynaud 3.1 (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1/tame-inertia-as-inverse-limit-of-roots-of-unity): both use sigma(pi_n) = i_n(sigma) pi_n, so chi_h is Raynaud's j_{q^h} followed by reduction. This agreement was checked on the page images of both sources.

nodes.title: Theorem 5.3(i): Ext^1(M(h; i), Sbar) = 0 for i of period h with 0 <= i_n <= q-1
nodes.statement: Assume k algebraically closed. Let i : Z/hZ -> Z have period h with 0 <= i_n <= q-1 for all n, and M = M(h; i). Then Ext^1_{MFtildecal}(M, Sbar) = 0.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed
0 <= i_n <= q-1 and i of exact period h
proofSteps: Replace Sbar by Ttilde (Proposition 5.5). Proposition 5.9 identifies Ttilde with the polynomial ring (A^tau/pi A^tau)[xi] with an explicit filtration and explicit phi^i_T; G acts on A^tau/pi A^tau and trivially on xi.

5.10: an extension of M by Ttilde is trivial iff the system (1) u_m in Ttilde^{i_m}, phi^{i_m}_T(u_m) - u_{m-1} = d_{m-1} is solvable for all d; by F_{q^h}-linearity reduce to one nonzero d, then compare coefficients of xi^j to reduce to the degree 0 and 1 equations.

Lemma 5.11 for M != M(1; q-1), case (i): i_0 != q-1, or i_1 = 0, or v(dhat) >= q^{-1} v(pi) for a lift dhat of d. Consider the equations (3) pi^{-i_m} X_m^q - X_{m-1} = 0 (m != 1) and pi^{-i_1} X_1^q - X_0 = dhat. Eliminating X_m for m != 0, with i = i_1 + q i_2 + ... + q^{h-2} i_{h-1} + q^{h-1} i_0, gives (4) X_0^{q^h} - pi^i X_0 - pi^i dhat = 0. This has a solution ahat_0 in Abar with v(ahat_0) >= q^{-h}(i v(pi) + v(dhat)), and the valuation estimates show its reduction solves (2).

Case (ii): i_0 = q-1, i_1 != 0 and v(dhat) < q^{-1} v(pi). Choose a' with dhat = pi^{-i_1}(a')^q and change variables, which splits the system into one of type (2) with d replaced by d' (solvable by (i)) and one where the index q-1 moves to i_{-1}. nodes.title: The restricted subcategories MF_tor^{f,q'} (no quotient N = N^{q-1}) and MF_tor^{f,q''} (no subobject N^1 = 0)
nodes.statement: MF_tor^{f,q'} is the full subcategory of MF_tor^{f,q} of objects admitting no nontrivial quotient N with N = N^{q-1}. MF_tor^{f,q''} is the full subcategory of objects admitting no nontrivial subobject N with N^1 = 0. Theorem 6.1(i): for an exact sequence 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0 of MF_tor^{f,q}, M is in MF_tor^{f,q'} (resp. MF_tor^{f,q''}) iff M' and M'' are. When k is algebraically closed, M is in MF_tor^{f,q'} (resp. MF_tor^{f,q''}) iff no Jordan-Hoelder quotient of M is isomorphic to M(1; q-1) (resp. M(1; 0)).
hypotheses: objects of MF_tor^{f,q}; for the Jordan-Hoelder characterization, k algebraically closed
proofSteps: 6.2: the base change M -> A' (x)_A M to an algebraically closed residue field is exact and faithful, so (i) reduces to k algebraically closed.

Lemma 6.3 (k algebraically closed, simple M in MF_tor^{f,q}): (i) if M != M(1; 0) then Ext^1(M(1; 0), M) = 0; (ii) if M != M(1; q-1) then Ext^1(M, M(1; q-1)) = 0. Both reduce to solving the linear systems epsilon(m) lambda_m^q - lambda_{m-1} = -mu_{m-1} and epsilon'(m) beta_m^q - beta_{m-1} = -gamma_{m-1} in k, where epsilon(m) = 0 if i_m != 0 and 1 if i_m = 0 (resp. epsilon'(m) = 0 if i_m != q-1 and 1 if i_m = q-1).

6.4: Ext^1(M(1; q-1), M(1; q-1)) = 0 in the category of objects killed by pi, so N with N^{q-1} = N is a direct sum of copies of M(1; q-1). With Lemma 6.3 and devissage, Ext^1(M, M(1; q-1)) = 0 for every M without such a Jordan-Hoelder quotient. Hence having a Jordan-Hoelder quotient isomorphic to M(1; q-1) is equivalent to having a nontrivial quotient N with N^{q-1} = N. The case of MF_tor^{f,q''} and M(1; 0) is "analogous".

nodes.title: Theorem 6.1(ii) on MF_tor^{f,q'}: U_S is fully faithful on objects without a quotient N = N^{q-1}
nodes.statement: The restriction of U_S to MF_tor^{f,q'} is fully faithful: for M, N in MF_tor^{f,q'}, Hom_MF(M, N) -> Hom_{O[G]}(U_S(N), U_S(M)) is bijective.

proofSteps: 6.2: reduce to k algebraically closed. Over A' = W(kbar) (x) A, Hom_MF(M, N) = (Hom_{MF'}(A' (x) M, A' (x) N))^G and U_S(M) = U_{S'}(A' (x) M); faithfulness forces a Galois-equivariant morphism upstairs to be G-invariant.

6.5: U_S is exact and faithful (Theorem 3.3). For simple objects, Hom(M, N) = 0 if M != N and End(M(h; i)) = F_{q^h}; Theorem 5.3 gives the same for the Galois modules inside MF_tor^{f,q'}. By induction on lengths and long exact Ext sequences, it suffices that Ext^1_MF(M, N) -> Ext^1_{O[G]}(U_S(N), U_S(M)) is injective for simple M, N; extensions not killed by pi have Galois modules not killed by pi, hence nonsplit.

Proposition 6.7: for M in MF_tor^{f,q'} with H the kernel of the G-action on U_S(M) and L inside Kbar, U_{S,L}(M) = U_S(M) iff L contains Kbar^H. The proof induces on length using Lemma 6.8, a Hensel-type lifting of solutions of the congruence system (1) to equations in Abar, which needs M(h; i) != M(1; q-1) so that some epsilon(i_m) = 0.

Proposition 6.10: with L the maximal tamely ramified extension, U_{S,L}(M) = U_S(M) iff M is semisimple. T_L contains T_{L,ss}, spanned by the omega_rho, which is a direct sum of one representative of each simple object, and Hom(M, Theta_L) = 0 for the quotient Theta_L.

6.11: if 0 -> N -> A -> M -> 0 with M, N simple has split Galois sequence, then H = Gal(Kbar/L) acts trivially on U_S(A) (Proposition 6.10 for M and N), so U_S(A) = U_{S,L}(A) (Proposition 6.7), so A is semisimple (Proposition 6.10) and the extension splits. nodes.statement: MF_{K/E}: finite-dimensional K-vector spaces Delta with a bijective tau-semilinear Phi and a decreasing, exhaustive, separated filtration by K-subspaces; morphisms commute with Phi and respect filtrations. It is E-linear, with tensor product, internal Hom, duals and a unit (7.2), and for E = Q_p it is Fontaine's MF_K of [F1] 1.2. Invariants (7.3): t_H(Delta) = i for a line with Delta^i = Delta, Delta^{i+1} = 0; t_N(Delta) = v_pi(a) for a line with Phi d = a d (v_pi(pi) = 1); both extended by top exterior powers and additive in short exact sequences. MF^f_{K/E} consists of Delta with t_H(Delta) = t_N(Delta) and t_H(Delta') <= t_N(Delta') for every Phi-stable subspace Delta' with induced structure. Proposition 7.5: MF^f_{K/E} is abelian, with kernels and cokernels computed in MF_{K/E}; it is stable under duals; a subobject (resp. quotient) of an object of MF^f_{K/E} lies in it iff t_H = t_N for it; and two-out-of-three holds for short exact sequences.

nodes.statement: A lattice M of Delta in MF_{K/E} (finitely generated A-submodule with K (x) M = Delta), with M^i = M intersect Delta^i, is strongly divisible if sum_i pi^{-i} Phi(M^i) = M. Proposition 7.8: a finite-dimensional Delta in MF_{K/E} admits a strongly divisible lattice iff Delta is in MF^f_{K/E}. In that case a lattice M is strongly divisible iff sum_i pi^{-i} Phi(M^i) is contained in M. Corollary 7.9: MF^f_{K/E} is stable under tensor product. Remark 7.10(b): every lattice M of Delta is contained in a smallest strongly divisible lattice and contains a largest one.

for E = Q_p the notion is Laffaille's "reseau adapte" of [L1]

7.9: M_1 (x) M_2 is strongly divisible in Delta_1 (x) Delta_2.

nodes.title: Strongly divisible lattices as finitely generated objects of MF with conditions (fd)_1-(fd)_3, and their reductions M_n = Coker pi^n
nodes.statement: MF^f_{/O} has objects (Delta, M) with Delta in MF^f_{K/E} and M a strongly divisible lattice, and morphisms mapping lattices to lattices. It is additive O-linear, and Hom(Delta, Delta') = E (x)_O Hom((Delta, M), (Delta', M')). The functor (Delta, M) -> M, with M^i = M intersect Delta^i and phi^i_M = pi^{-i} Phi, identifies MF^f_{/O} with the full subcategory of MF of finitely generated objects satisfying (fd)_1 M torsion free, (fd)_2 each M^i a direct factor of M, and (fd)_3 sum Im phi^i_M = M. Remark 7.13: (fd)_1 holds iff pi_M is a monomorphism in MFcal; (fd)_2 holds iff the cokernel of pi_M in MFcal is a filtered module; given (fd)_1, (fd)_3 holds iff that cokernel lies in MF_tor. For every n >= 1, M_n = Coker pi^n_M lies in MF_tor, and M = lim M_n. If M^0 = M and M^q = 0, the M_n lie in MF_tor^{f,q}.

nodes.title: Proposition 7.15(i): U_S on strongly divisible lattices MF^{f,q}_{/O} is exact, faithful, and preserves rank
nodes.statement: Let MF^{f,q}_{/O} be the full subcategory of MF^f_{/O} of M with M^0 = M and M^q = 0, and Rep_O(G) the category of finite free O-modules with continuous linear G-action. For M in MF^{f,q}_{/O} with reductions M_n, each U_S(M_n) is a free O/pi^n-module of rank h = rank_A M, identified with Hom(M_n, S_infinity) = Hom(M, S_n). The epimorphisms U_S(M_{n+1}) -> U_S(M_n) induced by pi : M_n -> M_{n+1} give U_S(M) := lim U_S(M_n) = Hom_MF(M, Shat), where Shat is the p-adic completion of S. The resulting contravariant functor U_S : MF^{f,q}_{/O} -> Rep_O(G) is exact and faithful with rank_O U_S(M) = rank_A M.
hypotheses: M a strongly divisible lattice object with M^0 = M and M^q = 0
proofSteps: 7.14: apply Theorem 3.3 to each M_n (lengths, exactness) and pass to the limit; the authors state that the proposition "results from Theorems 3.3 and 6.1".

nodes.title: The rational functor U_{S_K}(Delta) = Hom(Delta, Shat_K): dimension equality and injectivity of the evaluation map
nodes.statement: Let Shat_K = K (x)_A Shat with the filtration and Phi(a (x) x) = a^tau (x) phi^0_S(x), an object of MF_{K/E}, and let MF^{f,q}_{K/E} be the objects of MF^f_{K/E} with Delta^0 = Delta and Delta^q = 0. The contravariant E-linear functor U_{S_K} : MF^{f,q}_{K/E} -> Rep_E(G) is U_{S_K}(Delta) = Hom_{MF_{K/E}}(Delta, Shat_K). Proposition 7.17: for every Delta in MF^{f,q}_{K/E}, (i) dim_E U_{S_K}(Delta) = dim_K Delta; (ii) the canonical map Delta -> Hom_{E[G]}(U_{S_K}(Delta), Shat_K) is injective.

proofSteps: Choose a strongly divisible lattice M of Delta (Proposition 7.8).
(i) follows from rank_O U_S(M) = rank_A M (Proposition 7.15(i)).

(ii) With Mhat = Hom_{O[G]}(U_S(M), Shat) and xi : M -> Mhat the evaluation, the canonical map is xi_K. For each n the reduction xi_n : M_n -> Mhat/pi^n Mhat composed with the inclusion into Hom_{O[G]}(U_S(M_n), T_infinity) is injective by Proposition 5.15, so Ker xi lies in pi^n M for all n and xi, xi_K are injective.

nodes.title: Theorem 8.4(ii): for E = Q_p, U_{S_K} is naturally equivalent to the dual V_B^* of Fontaine's V_B on MF^{f,p}_K
nodes.statement: Assume E = Q_p (so K = K_0, e = 1). Let B be the Barsotti-Tate ring of [F2], and V_B^* : MF_{K,B} -> Rep(G) the contravariant functor sending D to the dual of V_B(D). The functor U_{S_K} and the restriction of V_B^* to MF^{f,p}_K (weakly admissible D with D^0 = D and D^p = 0) are naturally equivalent. Remark 8.5: the restriction of Delta_S : U -> Hom_{Q_p[G]}(U, Shat_K) to the essential image of U_{S_K} is D_B(U^*), and is a quasi-inverse of the fully faithful functor U_{S_K}.
hypotheses: D weakly admissible with D^0 = D and D^p = 0

imports: the ring B of [F2], the identification of Shat_K with B^+_a of [F2] Section 4 (a = ideal of x in R with v_R(x) >= p), and the dimension criterion for B-admissibility ([F1] n. 3.2, Proposition 3.4.3)
proofSteps: Identify the K-algebra Shat_K, as a filtered Galois ring, with B^+_a of [F2] Section 4 (stated, not proved here).
For D in MF^{f,p}_K let V = U_{S_K}(D). By Proposition 7.17(ii), D -> Hom_{Q_p[G]}(V, Shat_K) is injective, so dim_K Hom(V, Shat_K) >= dim_K D = dim V.

Hom_{Q_p[G]}(V, Shat_K) = Hom(V, B^+_a) = (V^* (x) B^+_a)^G is a K-subspace of D_B(V^*) ([F2] Section 4), so dim D_B(V^*) >= dim V^*. By [F1] n. 3.2 equality holds, D = D_B(V^*), and V^* (hence V) is B-admissible ([F1] Proposition 3.4.3).
V = Hom_{MF_K}(D, Shat_K) = Hom(D, B^+_a) is a Q_p[G]-submodule of Hom_MF(D, B) = V_B^*(D) ([F2] Section 4); equal dimensions give V_B^*(D) = U_{S_K}(D).
acceptance: Covariance check: U_{S_K} is contravariant and V_B covariant; the comparison is with the dual V_B^*, so filtration jump i on a rank-one D gives the i-th power of the cyclotomic character in U_{S_K}(D), not its inverse (consistent with Theorem 5.3(iii) modulo p). Verify against the normalization of V_B in [F2] before exporting a Hodge-Tate sign convention.

nodes.title: Theorem 8.4(i): for K = K_0, a weakly admissible filtered module with filtration length < p is admissible
nodes.statement: Assume E = Q_p (K = K_0, e = 1). If D is a weakly admissible filtered module (in MF^f_K) and there is an integer j with D^j = D_K and D^{j+p} = 0, then D is B-admissible. In particular MF^{f,p}_K = MF^{f,p}_{K/Q_p} is a subcategory of MF_{K,B}.

D weakly admissible, with filtration jumps in [j, j+p-1] for some integer j
imports: [F1] Proposition 4.4.1 (one-dimensional weakly admissible modules are admissible) and stability of MF_{K,B} under tensor product

D_1 is B-admissible by the proof of part (ii) (Theorem 8.4(ii) node).
D_2 is B-admissible because it has dimension 1 ([F1], Proposition 4.4.1).
D = D_1 (x) D_2 is B-admissible because MF_{K,B} is stable under tensor product.

nodes.title: Finite Honda systems (L, M) and Fontaine's anti-equivalence LM from finite flat p-groups over W(k) (p odd, or unipotent)
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect of characteristic p, A = W(k), D_k = A[F, V] with FV = VF = p, F a = sigma(a) F, a V = V sigma(a). For a p-group J over k (finite flat commutative of p-power rank), its Dieudonne module M(J) is the D_k-submodule of covectors in CW(O_k(J)) that are primitive for the coproduct, and M is an anti-equivalence from p-groups over k to finite D_k-modules (9.2). A finite Honda system is a pair (L, M) with M a finite D_k-module and L an A-submodule with (SH_1) FM intersect L = pL, (SH_2) L/pL = M/FM, (SH_3) V injective on L; it is unipotent if V is nilpotent on M. These form abelian artinian categories SH^f and SH^{f,u}. For a p-group J over A, L(J) is the kernel of w_{O(J)} restricted to M(J_k) in CW(O(J)_k), and LM(J) = (L(J), M(J_k)) is a finite Honda system. LM is an anti-equivalence from p-groups over A to SH^f if p != 2, and from unipotent p-groups (connected Cartier dual) to SH^{f,u} for every p. For a p-adically separated complete A-algebra S, J(S) is the group of D_k-linear maps M -> CW(S_k) sending L into Ker w_S (9.6).
hypotheses: k perfect, A = W(k) (so e = 1)
p != 2 for the full anti-equivalence; unipotent objects for all p
proofSteps: Source status in Fontaine-Laffaille: 9.1-9.6 are recalls ("rappels"), with references to Fontaine [F3] (C. R. Acad. Sci. 280, 1975) and [F4] (Groupes p-divisibles sur les corps locaux).

Written proof located: Conrad (Compositio 1999), Section 1, writes out Fontaine's proof for e = 1. Theorem 1.1 (read here with proof) shows L/pL -> M/FM is an isomorphism and V is injective on L. Its steps are a membership criterion in M via w_R, then pL = FM intersect L, then surjectivity of L[p] (+) ker V -> M[p], then a length count with exactness of 0 -> M/VM -> M/pM -> M/FM -> 0. Theorem 1.4 (full faithfulness and essential surjectivity) was read as a statement only; its five-step proof was not read.
acceptance: The restriction at p = 2 is forced by mu_2 and Z/2Z over Z_2 having isomorphic generic fibres (Conrad p. 8).
Check that (SH_1) + (SH_2) is Conrad's single condition "L/pL -> M/FM is an isomorphism".

nodes.title: Propositions 9.9-9.10: finite Honda systems are equivalent to MF_tor^{f,2} (filtration in [0,1]) over W(k)
nodes.statement: Assume e = 1, r = 1 (tau = sigma, O = Z_p) and pi = p. Define I : SH^f -> MF_tor^{f,2} by: the A-module of I(L, M) is M_{sigma^{-1}}; the filtration is M for i <= 0, VL for i = 1, 0 for i >= 2; phi^0 = F and phi^1(x) = the unique y in L with x = V y (unique by (SH_3)). For M in MF_tor^{f,2}, 9.8 makes M_sigma a finite D_k-module via F = phi^0_M (= phi_M o alpha^0_M) and V = beta_M o phi_M^{-1}, using the bijection phi_M : Mtilde -> M_sigma and the canonical map beta_M : Mtilde -> M. Define H(M) = (L, M_sigma) with L = Im phi^1_M. Proposition 9.9: H(M) is a finite Honda system. Proposition 9.10: I induces an equivalence SH^f -> MF_tor^{f,2} with quasi-inverse H.

objects with M^0 = M, M^2 = 0

nodes.title: 9.11: ILM is an anti-equivalence from finite flat p-groups over W(k) to MF_tor^{f,2} (p odd), and from unipotent ones to MF_tor^{f,2'} (all p)
nodes.statement: Composing LM with I gives the contravariant additive functor ILM from p-groups over A = W(k) to MF_tor^{f,2}. A finite Honda system (L, M) is unipotent iff I(L, M) lies in MF_tor^{f,2'} (no nontrivial quotient N with N = N^1). nodes.title: Breuil's ring S (p-adic divided power envelope) and the categories (Mod/S), (Mod FI/S) of Breuil modules
nodes.statement: Kisin 2009 Section 1.1 standing hypotheses: p != 2, k a finite extension of F_p, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], K/K_0 finite totally ramified with uniformizer pi and Eisenstein polynomial E(u) over K_0. Scalpha is the p-adic completion of the divided power envelope of W[u] with respect to the kernel of s : W[u] -> O_K, u -> pi. Fil^1 Scalpha is the p-adic completion of the ideal generated by gamma_i(E(u)) = E(u)^i/i!. phi extends the Frobenius of W with phi(u) = u^p. Since phi(Fil^1 Scalpha) is contained in p Scalpha, one sets phi_1 = p^{-1} phi on Fil^1 Scalpha and c = phi_1(E(u)), a unit of Scalpha. '(Mod/Scalpha) consists of triples (Mcal, Fil^1 Mcal, phi_1) with Fil^1 Mcal containing Fil^1 Scalpha . Mcal and phi_1(s x) = c^{-1} phi_1(s) phi_1(E(u) x). It is an exact category, with sequences exact on modules and on Fil^1. (Mod FI/Scalpha): objects with Mcal isomorphic to a finite direct sum of Scalpha/p^{n_i} and with phi_1(Fil^1 Mcal) generating Mcal. (Mod/Scalpha): the smallest full subcategory containing the p-killed objects of (Mod FI/Scalpha) and closed under extensions.
hypotheses: k a finite extension of F_p (Kisin 2009 Section 1.1 standing assumption)
K/K_0 finite totally ramified, E(u) the Eisenstein polynomial of the fixed uniformizer pi
proofSteps: Construct Scalpha, Fil^1 Scalpha and phi, and check that the ideal (p, E(u)) is phi-stable because E(u) = u^e mod p, so phi extends continuously.
Define the three categories and the exact structure (recalled from Breuil [Br3], [Br4], [Br5]).
acceptance: Check that c = phi_1(E(u)) is a unit of Scalpha.
Record the dependence on the choice of uniformizer pi (through E(u) and the embedding u -> [pi] of 1.1.12).
