nodes.title: Breuil's theorem (Kisin 1.1.3) with Cartier duality (1.1.5, 1.1.7): (Mod/Scalpha) is equivalent to finite flat p-groups over O_K, p odd
nodes.statement: Assume p != 2 and k finite. Let (p-Gr/O_K) be the category of finite flat group schemes over O_K of p-power order, and (p-Gr/O_K)^fl its full subcategory of G such that every G[p^n] (as an fppf sheaf) is a finite flat group scheme. Theorem 1.1.3 (Breuil): there are quasi-inverse anti-equivalences Gr : (Mod/Scalpha) -> (p-Gr/O_K) and Mod : (p-Gr/O_K) -> (Mod/Scalpha), restricting to anti-equivalences (Mod FI/Scalpha) <-> (p-Gr/O_K)^fl, and preserving short exact sequences. Lemma 1.1.5: Cartier duality D preserves (p-Gr/O_K)^fl. Corollary 1.1.7: Mod^D = Mod o D and Gr^D = D o Gr are equivalences (Mod/Scalpha) <-> (p-Gr/O_K) and (Mod FI/Scalpha) <-> (p-Gr/O_K)^fl.
hypotheses: k finite
O_K the ring of integers of a finite totally ramified extension of K_0 = W(k)[1/p]
proofSteps: Theorem 1.1.3 is quoted from Breuil, Groupes p-divisibles, groupes finis et modules filtres [Br3], 4.2.1.6 and 4.2.2.5; Kisin gives no proof ("This is in [Br3, 4.2.1.6, 4.2.2.5]").

Lemma 1.1.5: for G in (p-Gr/O_K)^fl the fppf sequence 0 -> G[p^n] -> G -> G -> G/p^n G -> 0 (1.1.6) splits into two short exact sequences in (p-Gr/O_K), because p^n G = G/G[p^n] is finite flat and closed in G. Exactness of D then identifies D(G)[p^n] with D(G/p^n G), which is finite flat.
Corollary 1.1.7 composes 1.1.3 with D.
acceptance: p = 2 is excluded: the Breuil-module classification of 1.1.3 is not asserted by Kisin at p = 2 (see footnote to 2.2.16).
Check covariance: Gr is contravariant, and Gr^D is the covariant version used from 1.1.13 on.

These restrict to anti-equivalences Gr : (Mod FI/S) -> (p-Gr/O_K)^fl and Mod : (p-Gr/O_K)^fl -> (Mod FI/S). These functors preserve short exact sequences. Proof. This is in [Br3, 4.2.1.6, 4.2.2.5].

nodes.title: Kisin modules over S = W[[u]]: the categories (Mod/S), (Mod FI/S) and injectivity of 1 (x) phi
nodes.statement: Let S = W[[u]] with phi(u) = u^p and the Frobenius of W, and S_n = W_n[[u]]. '(Mod/S) consists of S-modules M with phi-semilinear phi : M -> M such that the cokernel of 1 (x) phi : phi^*(M) = S (x)_{phi,S} M -> M is killed by E(u); it is an exact category. (Mod FI/S) consists of those M isomorphic as S-modules to a finite direct sum of S_{n_i}; (Mod/S) is the smallest full subcategory containing the p-killed objects of (Mod FI/S) and closed under extensions. Lemma 1.1.9: for every M in (Mod/S), 1 (x) phi : phi^* M -> M is injective.
hypotheses: p != 2 and k finite (standing hypotheses of Section 1.1)
proofSteps: Lemma 1.1.9: by devissage reduce to M killed by p. Then M is free over S/pS of some rank r, and the determinant of 1 (x) phi divides u^{er} because its image contains u^e M; u^{er} is not a zero divisor in S/pS.

nodes.title: Proposition 1.1.11: M -> Mcal = Scalpha (x)_{phi,S} M is exact and fully faithful (Mod/S) -> (Mod/Scalpha), an equivalence on p-killed objects
nodes.statement: Regard Scalpha as an S-algebra via u -> u and let phi : S -> Scalpha be this map composed with phi. For M in (Mod/S) set Mcal = Scalpha (x)_{phi,S} M, with Fil^1 Mcal = {y : (1 (x) phi)(y) in Fil^1 Scalpha (x)_S M} and phi_1 the composite Fil^1 Mcal -> Fil^1 Scalpha (x)_S M -> Scalpha (x)_{phi,S} M = Mcal given by phi_1 (x) 1. Proposition 1.1.11: this induces exact, fully faithful functors (Mod/S) -> (Mod/Scalpha) and (Mod FI/S) -> (Mod FI/Scalpha), which are equivalences on the full subcategories of objects killed by p.
hypotheses: p != 2, k finite
proofSteps: Exactness on modules: Tor_1^S(Scalpha, M) = 0 because M is a successive extension of free S/pS-modules and Scalpha is p-torsion free.

Exactness on Fil^1: left exactness is formal. For surjectivity, alter x in Fil^1 Mcal'' by Fil^1 Scalpha . Mcal'' so that x comes from xtilde in phi^*(M''); since E(u) M surjects onto E(u) M'', Lemma 1.1.9 gives a preimage ytilde in phi^*(M) with (1 (x) phi)(ytilde) in E(u) M.
phi_1(Fil^1 Mcal) generates Mcal because it contains c (x) M.
Equivalence on p-killed objects: "The proof of [Br4, 3.3.2] shows that our functors induce equivalences" (imported, not reproduced).
Full faithfulness in general by devissage "as in [FoL, p. 584]", using the long exact Hom/Ext^1 sequences available in any exact category ([Qu, 2]).

nodes.title: Proposition 1.1.13: T(O_E (x)_S M)(1) is G_{K_infinity}-isomorphic to Gr^D(Mcal)(O_Kbar)
nodes.statement: Let R = lim O_Kbar/p (Frobenius transitions), theta : W(R) -> O_Cp, A_cris the p-adic completion of the divided power envelope of W(R) along ker(theta), and pi_n compatible p^n-th roots of pi with pibar = (pi_n) in R. u -> [pibar] embeds S into W(R) and extends to Scalpha into A_cris, compatibly with Frobenius. O_E is the p-adic completion of S[1/u], a DVR with residue field k((u)); O_{E^ur} is the ring of integers of its maximal unramified extension inside W(Fr R)[1/p], with completion O_{Ehat^ur}; and S^ur = O_{Ehat^ur} intersect W(R). With K_infinity = union K(pi_n), the functor T : Phi M_{O_E} -> Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_infinity}), M -> (O_{Ehat^ur} (x)_{O_E} M)^{phi = 1}, from finite etale phi-modules over O_E, is an equivalence of abelian categories. Proposition 1.1.13: for M in (Mod/S) with image Mcal in (Mod/Scalpha) there is a canonical G_{K_infinity}-isomorphism T(O_E (x)_S M)(1) -> Gr^D(Mcal)(O_Kbar)|_{G_{K_infinity}}.
hypotheses: p != 2, k finite; K_infinity/K is strictly APF ([Br1, 2.1.1]), which makes Fontaine's theory of the field of norms apply
imports: Fontaine, Representations p-adiques des corps locaux [Fo], A.1.2.6, A.1.2.7, A.3 and B.1.8.4; Breuil [Br2, 2.3.11], [Br3, 5.3.1], [Br4, 3.3.2]
proofSteps: Equivalence T : Phi M_{O_E} -> Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_infinity}) from [Fo, A.1.2.6] and the constructions of [Fo, A.3] (imported).
Since Gr^D(Mcal)(O_Kbar) = Hom(Gr(Mcal)(O_Kbar), Q_p/Z_p(1)), it suffices by [Fo, A.1.2.7] to give a canonical G_{K_infinity}-isomorphism Hom_{S,phi}(M, E^ur/O_{E^ur}) -> Gr(Mcal)(O_Kbar).

By [Fo, B.1.8.4], Hom_{S,phi}(M, S^ur[1/p]/S^ur) -> Hom_{S,phi}(M, E^ur/O_{E^ur}) is an isomorphism, so the left side is exact in M. By [Br2, 2.3.11] and [Br3, 5.3.1], Gr(Mcal)(O_Kbar) = Hom_{Scalpha,phi_1,Fil^1}(Mcal, A_cris[1/p]/A_cris).
The map (1.1.14) f -> (1 (x) phi) o (1 (x) f) between the two Hom groups is compatible and both sides are exact, so by devissage reduce to p M = 0, where it is [Br4, 3.3.2] and its proof.

nodes.statement: For M in (Mod/S) with image Mcal, Gr^D(Mcal) is etale (resp. of multiplicative type) iff 1 (x) phi : phi^* M -> M has image equal to E(u) M (resp. is an isomorphism). nodes.title: Lemma 1.2.2-1.2.3: projectivity and base change for Kisin modules with coefficients (Mod FI/S)_A
nodes.statement: For a Z_p-algebra A set S_A = S (x)_{Z_p} A. (Mod FI/S)_A is the category of objects of '(Mod/S) with an A-action that are finite projective S_A-modules; (Mod FI/Scalpha)_A requires Mcal finite projective over Scalpha_A, Mcal/Fil^1 Mcal finite projective over A, and phi_1 generating. Lemma 1.2.2: for M in (Mod FI/S)_A, (1) 1 (x) phi : phi^*(M) -> M is injective; (2) its cokernel is a finite projective A-module; (3) (1 (x) phi)(phi^* M)/E(u)M is a finite projective A-module; (4) if A is finite, M is locally on Spec A a finite free S_A-module. Lemma 1.2.3: base change - (x)_A A' along A -> A' preserves both categories.
hypotheses: A a Z_p-algebra (finite for (4) and for the Scalpha-version)
proofSteps: (1): reduce to A finitely generated and M of constant rank r; 1 (x) phi is a map of free modules of equal rank whose image contains E(u)M, so its determinant divides E(u)^r, which is a non-zero-divisor because S/E(u)^r is Z_p-flat. The same argument after (x)_A A/I gives A-flatness of the cokernel.
(2): the cokernel is a finite quotient of the finite O_K (x) A-module M/E(u)M and A-flat, hence A-projective.
(3): from the exact sequence 0 -> (1 (x) phi)(phi^* M)/E(u)M -> M/E(u)M -> M/(1 (x) phi)(phi^* M) -> 0.
(4): reduce to A a finite field; S_A has finitely many maximal ideals, permuted transitively by phi, and the injectivity (1) forces the local ranks to be equal.
acceptance: Check (4) fails without the Frobenius transitivity argument, e.g. why a projective S_A-module need not be free when A is a product of fields.

nodes.title: Proposition 1.2.11: Kisin modules with finite coefficients have a maximal multiplicative subobject and a maximal etale quotient, compatible with base change and duality
nodes.statement: Let A be finite and M_A in (Mod FI/S)_A. The dual M_A^vee = Hom_{S_A}(M_A, S_A) has Frobenius defined via 1 (x) phi (1.2.10); M_A is etale iff M_A^vee is multiplicative, and double duality holds in (Mod FI/S)_A. Proposition 1.2.11: there exist a maximal multiplicative subobject M_A^m of M_A and a maximal etale quotient M_A^et such that (1) M_A/M_A^m and Ker(M_A -> M_A^et) lie in (Mod FI/S)_A; (2) for every finite A-algebra B, (M_A (x)_A B)^m = M_A^m (x)_A B and (M_A (x)_A B)^et = M_A^et (x)_A B; (3) (M_A^m)^vee = (M_A^vee)^et and (M_A^et)^vee = (M_A^vee)^m.
hypotheses: A finite Z_p-algebra
p != 2, k finite
proofSteps: Since 1 (x) phi is injective (1.2.2(1)) and phi on S is flat, the iterates 1 (x) phi^r : (phi^*)^r(M_A) -> M_A are injective. Set M_A^m to be the intersection over r >= 1 of (phi^*)^r M_A.
M_A/M_A^m is u-torsion free: x in M_A is divisible by u iff phi^i(x) is for large i, and Artin-Rees gives convergence.

Write M_A/uM_A = (M_A/uM_A)^nil (+) (M_A/uM_A)^unit, with phi nilpotent on the first factor and bijective on the second. M_A^m/uM_A^m is identified with the unit part by a convergence argument, so it is a direct summand, projective over S_A/uS_A and then free after localizing. Nakayama gives (S_A)^d = M_A^m.
Base change: M_A/M_A^m is projective over S_A, and the reductions mod u of (M_A/M_A^m) (x) B and M_B/M_B^m are both (M_B/uM_B)^nil of the same B-rank.
Define M_A^et := ((M_A^vee)^m)^vee; duality yields its maximality and (2)-(3).
acceptance: Rank two check: a nonsplit extension of an etale by a multiplicative rank-one object has M^m the multiplicative line and M^et the etale quotient.

nodes.title: Corollary 2.2.22 (Breuil's conjecture for p > 2): (Mod FI/S)_{Z_p} is equivalent to p-divisible groups over O_K
nodes.statement: Assume p > 2 and k finite. The category (Mod FI/S)_{Z_p} of finite free S-modules M with phi-semilinear phi such that the image of 1 (x) phi contains E(u)M is equivalent to the category of p-divisible groups over O_K.
hypotheses: p > 2 (Section 1.1 assumption p != 2)
k finite
O_K totally ramified over W(k)[1/p]
proofSteps: By [Br3, 4.2.2.9] (imported), (Mod FI/Scalpha)_{Z_p} is anti-equivalent to p-divisible groups over O_K; composing with Cartier duality gives an equivalence.
Applying Lemma 1.2.4 with A = Z/p^n and passing to the limit gives a fully faithful functor (Mod FI/S)_{Z_p} -> (Mod FI/Scalpha)_{Z_p}.

Essential surjectivity: for Mcal in (Mod FI/Scalpha)_{Z_p}, Lemma 1.2.5 lifts Mcal_1 = Mcal/p to M_1 in (Mod FI/S)_{F_p}. Then (1 (x) phi)(phi^* M_1)/u^e M_1 = (Mcal/Fil^1 Mcal) (x) Z/p is free over k[[u]]/u^e = O_K/p, so Proposition 2.2.19 applies with M_{F_p} = M_1.

Proposition 2.2.19: M_A -> Scalpha (x)_{phi,S} M_A is an equivalence of groupoids D_{M_{F_p}} -> D_{Mcal_{F_p}} over artinian Z_p-algebras. Full faithfulness comes from 1.2.4. For bijectivity on isomorphism classes, both groupoids have Noetherian versal deformation rings (Lemma 2.2.18, via Schlessinger and [Br3, 2.1.2.2]); the map of versal rings is an isomorphism modulo p (Lemma 1.2.5) and hence an isomorphism once R^ver_{M_{F_p}} is Z_p-flat.

Z_p-flatness of R^ver_{M_{F_p}}: in a Cartesian diagram of functors, formal smoothness of Dtilde_{M} -> Dbar_{M} (Proposition 2.2.11) and freeness of the modules L_A (Lemma 2.2.17) give formal smoothness over Z_p.

nodes.title: Kisin modules of height 1 over a perfect residue field and T_S(M) = Hom_{phi,S}(M, W(R)), fully faithful into G_{K_infinity}-lattices
nodes.statement: Liu 2013 setup: k perfect of characteristic p (any p), K/K_0 finite totally ramified, E(u) the Eisenstein polynomial of pi, S = W(k)[[u]]. Mod^{1,fr}_{/S} is the category of finite free S-modules M with phi-semilinear phi_M such that the cokernel of 1 (x) phi_M : S (x)_{phi,S} M -> M is killed by E(u) (Kisin modules of height 1). For M in Mod^{1,fr}_{/S}, T_S(M) = Hom_{phi,S}(M, W(R)) is a Z_p[G_infinity]-module, finite free with rank_{Z_p} T_S(M) = rank_S M. The functor T_S : Mod^{1,fr}_{/S} -> Rep_{Z_p}(G_infinity) is fully faithful. Remark 2.1.1: the definition agrees with Hom_{phi,S}(M, S^ur).
hypotheses: k perfect (not necessarily finite); any prime p
imports: rank statement [Kis06, Corollary 2.1.4]; full faithfulness [Kis06, Proposition 2.1.12] or [Liu07, Corollary 4.2.6]; comparison of the two definitions [CL11, Lemma 2.2.1]
proofSteps: All three properties are recalled from [Kis06], [Liu07] and [CL11] and not proved in Liu 2013.
acceptance: For p > 2 and k finite, compare Mod^{1,fr}_{/S} with Kisin 2009's (Mod FI/S)_{Z_p}: both are finite free S-modules with E(u)-height at most 1.

nodes.title: Liu Lemma 2.2.3: the Breuil module Mcal = Scalpha (x)_{phi,S} M has a unique monodromy N with N(M) in I_+Scalpha . Mcal, and N^i(M) in u^p Mtilde
nodes.statement: For M in Mod^{1,fr}_{/S}, Mcal = Scalpha (x)_{phi,S} M with Fil^1 Mcal and phi_1 as in Kisin 1.1.10 satisfies axioms (1)-(3) of a Breuil module. Let N_Scalpha be the K_0-derivation with N(u) = -u and I_+Scalpha = Scalpha intersect u K_0[[u]]. (1) There is a unique monodromy operator N on Mcal (W(k)-linear, N(s m) = N_Scalpha(s) m + s N(m), phi_1(E(u)N(x)) = c_1 N(phi_1(x)) for x in Fil^1 Mcal) with N(M) contained in I_+Scalpha . Mcal. (2) N^i(M) is contained in u^p Mtilde for all i >= 1, where Mtilde is the phi(S)-submodule of Mcal generated by M.
hypotheses: any p (Liu notes that Breuil's proof [Bre00, Prop. 5.1.3] does not use p > 2 or k finite)
M in Mod^{1,fr}_{/S}
proofSteps: (1): choose x_1, ..., x_d in Fil^1 Mcal with e_i = phi_1(x_i) a basis of Mcal; define derivations N_0(e_i) = 0 and N_n(e_i) = c_1^{-1} phi_1(E(u) N_{n-1}(x_i)).
By induction (N_n - N_{n-1})(Mcal) lies in u^{p^n} Mcal, using N_Scalpha(Scalpha) in u Scalpha. So N_n converges to a derivation N satisfying the Frobenius compatibility.
Uniqueness: N - N' is S-linear and satisfies a fixed-point relation with a matrix A over phi(I_+Scalpha), forcing N = N'.

(2): choose x_i in (Scalpha (x)_{phi,S} M) intersect Fil^1 Mcal with e_i = phi_1(x_i) = c_1 f_i a basis of Mtilde; the construction gives N(e_i) in u^p Mtilde, and N(c_1^{-1}) in u^p K_0[[u^p]], hence N(f_i) in u^p Mtilde.
acceptance: Check on M = S with phi = 1 that N = 0 on M.

nodes.title: Liu Proposition 2.2.2 and construction: M -> Q_p (x) lambda(T_S(M)) inside Ttilde_cris(Mcal) is crystalline with Hodge-Tate weights in {0, 1}
nodes.statement: For M in Mod^{1,fr}_{/S}, use N (Lemma 2.2.3) to define the A_cris-semilinear G_K-action (2.2.1) g(a (x) x) = sum_i g(a) gamma_i(-log[epsilon(g)]) (x) N^i(x) on A_cris (x)_Scalpha Mcal, where epsilon(g) = g(pibar)/pibar. This action preserves phi and Fil^1. Set Ttilde_cris(Mcal) = Hom_{A_cris, phi, Fil^1}(A_cris (x)_Scalpha Mcal, A_cris) with G_K-action. Then Q_p (x) Ttilde_cris(Mcal) is crystalline with Hodge-Tate weights in {0, 1}. The map lambda : T_S(M) -> Ttilde_cris(Mcal), lambda(f)(a (x) m) = a phi(f(m)), is injective and G_infinity-equivariant, and lambda[1/p] is an isomorphism. Proposition 2.2.2: M -> iota(M) := Q_p (x) lambda(T_S(M)) is a functor Mod^{1,fr}_{/S} -> Rep^{cris,1}_{Q_p} inducing an anti-equivalence on isogeny categories. Remark 2.2.4: for p > 2, lambda' : T_S(M) -> T_cris(Mcal) = Hom_{Scalpha,phi,Fil^1}(Mcal, A_cris) is a Z_p[G_infinity]-isomorphism ([Liu08, Lemma 3.3.4]); for p = 2 it need not be ([Liu07, Example 5.3.3]). Remark 2.2.5: iota is contravariant, and iota'(M) = iota(M)^*(1) is isomorphic to iota(M^vee).
hypotheses: any p; k perfect

imports: [Liu08, Lemma 5.1.1] (the G-action preserves phi and Fil^1); [Liu08, Lemma 5.2.1] (Q_p (x) Ttilde_cris(Mcal) = V_st(D)); [Bre02, Proposition 2.2.5] (V_st(D) semistable with weights in {0, 1}); [Bre97] (recovering N_D from N mod I_+Scalpha); [Kis06, Proposition 2.2.2] for the original proof of 2.2.2
proofSteps: Construct the G_K-action (2.2.1) from N; it preserves phi and Fil^1 as in [Liu08, Lemma 5.1.1].

Q_p (x) Ttilde_cris(Mcal) is V_st(D) for D = Q_p (x) Mcal ([Liu08, 5.2.1]), which is semistable with weights in {0, 1} ([Bre02, 2.2.5]). Since N(M) is in u^p Mtilde (Lemma 2.2.3), N_D = 0 by [Bre97], so V_st(D) is crystalline.
lambda is injective and G_infinity-compatible; dimensions agree (dim V_st(D) = dim_{K_0} D = rank M = rank T_S(M)), so lambda[1/p] is an isomorphism.
acceptance: Covariance check (Remark 2.2.5): the contravariant iota and the covariant iota' = iota(-)^*(1) differ by dual and cyclotomic twist; fix which one is exported before comparing with Kisin 1.1.13's T(O_E (x) M)(1) and Gr^D.

nodes.title: Liu Propositions 3.1.1-3.1.2 and Corollary 3.1.3: T_S(M) embeds into J(M) = Hom_{S,phi}(M, W(R)/utW(R)), which carries a natural G_K-action extending the G_infinity-action
nodes.statement: Let I^[1] be the ideal of W(R) of x with phi^m(x) in Fil^1 B^+_cris for all m >= 1; it is principal, generated by [epsilon] - 1 ([Fon94a, Prop. 5.1.3]), and also by phi(t) for t in W(R) with phi(t) = c_0^{-1} E(u) t and t != 0 mod p ([Liu07, Ex. 2.3.5], [Liu10, proof of Lemma 3.2.2]); here p c_0 is the constant term of E(u). Set J'(M) = Hom_{S,phi}(M, W(R)/uI^[1]) and J(M) = Hom_{S,phi}(M, W(R)/utW(R)), with natural maps eta' : T_S(M) -> J'(M), eta : T_S(M) -> J(M) and mu : J'(M) -> J(M). Proposition 3.1.1: eta and eta' are injective and mu(J'(M)) = eta(T_S(M)). Proposition 3.1.2: J(M) and J'(M) have natural G_K-actions, so T_S(M) acquires a G_K-action compatible with its G_infinity-action. Corollary 3.1.3: every Z_p[G_infinity]-morphism T_S(M) -> T_S(N) is a Z_p[G_K]-morphism.
hypotheses: any p, k perfect
M, N in Mod^{1,fr}_{/S}
proofSteps: 3.1.1(1): if h is in Ker(eta), its coordinate vector X = utY satisfies phi(X) = XA. Using a matrix B with AB = BA = E(u) Id and phi(t) = c_0^{-1} E(u) t, iterate Y = c_0^{-1} u^{p-1} phi(Y) B to put Y in the intersection of the u^n W(R), which is 0.
3.1.1(2): for h in J'(M) with lift X, solve phi(X + utZ) = (X + utZ)A. This reduces to Z = c_0^{-1} Y B + c_0^{-1} u^{p-1} phi(Z) B (3.1.3), whose iteration converges u-adically.

3.1.2: uI^[1] and utW(R) are G-stable (g(u) - u = u([epsilon(g)] - 1) lies in uI^[1]; phi(utW(R)) lies in u^p I^[1], which is G-stable, and phi is bijective on W(R)), so g acts on J'(M) and J(M) preserving S-linearity and phi.
3.1.3: by full faithfulness of T_S, f = T_S(f) for a morphism f : N -> M, and f induces maps on J' and J compatible with the G-actions.
acceptance: Check that the G-action on T_S(M) for M = S (phi = 1) is trivial and for the multiplicative rank-one object is the cyclotomic character twist predicted by iota.

nodes.title: Liu Lemma 3.2.2: for x in B^+_cris, u x in W(R) implies x in W(R), including p = 2
nodes.statement: Let x be in B^+_cris with u x in W(R), where u acts as [pibar]. Then x is in W(R).
hypotheses: any p (the dyadic case needs a separate choice of indices)
proofSteps: Fact: if w is in W(R) and p^s divides u w in W(R), then p^s divides w, because u mod p = pibar != 0 and R is a domain.

Case x in A_cris: write x = sum a_i E(u)^i/i! with a_i in W(R) and n_i = v_p(i!). Then p^{n_i} u x = u xtilde_i + ztilde_i with xtilde_i in W(R) and ztilde_i in Fil^{i+1} A_cris intersect W(R) = E(u)^{i+1} W(R). Writing E(u)^{i+1} = p^{i+1} b_i + u w_i gives y = u x(i) + p^{i+1-n_i} z(i) with x(i), z(i) in W(R).
Choose i_m with i_m + 1 - n_{i_m} -> infinity: for p > 2 take i_m = m (n_i <= i/(p-1)); for p = 2 take i_m = 2^m - 1, where v_2((2^m - 1)!) = 2^m - m - 1 gives i_m + 1 - n_{i_m} = m + 1.
Case x in B^+_cris with p^s x in A_cris: then p^s x is in W(R) by the first case, and the Fact gives x in W(R).

Claim: by (2.2.1) and Lemma 2.2.3, g(1 (x) e_i) = sum_j gamma_j(-log[epsilon(g)]) (x) N^j(1 (x) e_i) = 1 (x) e_i mod u^p (I^[1] B^+_cris) Mhat. The matrix A of g - 1 has entries in Rhat, contained in W(R), and in u^p I^[1] B^+_cris, hence by Lemma 3.2.2 in u^p I^[1] = u^p phi(t) W(R).

nodes.title: Fontaine's normalization of ramification groups: i_{L/K}, G_(i), u_{L/K}, G^(u) = G^{u-1} and the dictionary with Serre
nodes.statement: Let K be complete for a discrete valuation with perfect residue field of characteristic p, v_K normalized by v_K(K^*) = Z and extended to algebraic extensions. For L/K finite Galois with group G and g in G, let a_g be the ideal of O_L generated by the (g-1)x for x in O_L, and i_{L/K}(g) = v_K(a_g) (so e_{L/K} i_{L/K}(g) is in N union {infinity}). Put G_(i) = {g : i_{L/K}(g) >= i}, phi_{L/K}(i) = sum_{g in G} min{i, i_{L/K}(g)} (piecewise linear, increasing, bijective), u_{L/K}(g) = phi_{L/K}(i_{L/K}(g)) and G^(u) = {g : u_{L/K}(g) >= u}. Then G^(u) = G_(psi_{L/K}(u)). Set i_{L/K} = sup_{g != 1} i_{L/K}(g) and u_{L/K} = sup_{g != 1} u_{L/K}(g), the largest i (resp. u) with G_(i) != 1 (resp. G^(u) != 1); u_{L/K} = phi_{L/K}(i_{L/K}). Dictionary with Serre, Corps locaux Ch. IV (Remark 1.2(i)): G_j = G_((j+1)/e_{L/K}) and G^v = G^(v+1), phi_{L/K}(j) = phitilde((j+1)/e_{L/K}) - 1 and psi_{L/K}(v) = e_{L/K} psitilde(v+1) - 1. Remark 1.2(ii): the images of G'^(u) in quotients are G^(u) (Serre Prop. 14, p. 81), so G_K^(u) = lim Gal(L/K)^(u) is defined for Kbar/K. u_{L/K} is the smallest u such that G_K^(u+epsilon) is contained in Gal(Kbar/L) for all epsilon > 0.
hypotheses: K complete discretely valued, perfect residue field of characteristic p != 0
L/K finite Galois (then infinite Galois by passage to the limit)
proofSteps: Definitions 1.1; the properties of phi, psi and the quotient compatibility are imported from Serre, Corps locaux [Se1], Chapter IV (Prop. 14, p. 81).
acceptance: Convention check: Serre's upper numbering G^v corresponds to Fontaine's G^(v+1); a bound "G^(u) acts trivially for u > e(n + 1/(p-1))" is "G^v acts trivially for v > e(n + 1/(p-1)) - 1" in Serre's numbering. Export this translation explicitly to ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01 before SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCases uses it.
Tame extension check: for L/K tamely and totally ramified, u_{L/K} = 1 (used in the proof of Proposition 1.5(ii)).

nodes.title: Proposition 1.3: v_K(D_{L/K}) = u_{L/K} - i_{L/K}
nodes.statement: For L/K finite Galois with different D_{L/K}, v_K(D_{L/K}) = u_{L/K} - i_{L/K}.
hypotheses: L/K finite Galois; the valuations and ramification functions of 1.1
proofSteps: By Serre, Corps locaux, Prop. 4, p. 72: v_K(D_{L/K}) = sum_{g != 1} i_{L/K}(g) = sum_{g in G} min{i_{L/K}, i_{L/K}(g)} - i_{L/K} = phi_{L/K}(i_{L/K}) - i_{L/K} = u_{L/K} - i_{L/K}.
acceptance: Worked check: L = Q_2(i) over Q_2, alpha = i. Then i_{L/K}(sigma) = v_K(-2i) = 1, so i_{L/K} = 1, u_{L/K} = phi(1) = 2, and v_K(D_{L/K}) = v_K(P'(i)) = v_K(2i) = 1 = u - i.

nodes.title: Propositions 1.4-1.5: approximate O_K-points modulo a^m_{E/K} force a K-embedding of L when m > u_{L/K}, and conversely
nodes.statement: Let L/K be finite Galois, O_L = O_K[alpha] with minimal polynomial P. Proposition 1.4: for beta in an algebraic extension containing L, with i = sup_g v_K(beta - g alpha) and u = v_K(P(beta)), one has u = phi_{L/K}(i) and i = psi_{L/K}(u). Proposition 1.5: for m >= 0 real consider (P_m): for every algebraic extension E of K, if there is an O_K-algebra homomorphism O_L -> O_E/a^m_{E/K} (a^m_{E/K} = elements of valuation >= m), then there is a K-embedding of L into E. Then (i) if m > u_{L/K}, (P_m) holds; (ii) if (P_m) holds, then m > u_{L/K} - e_{L/K}^{-1}.
hypotheses: L/K finite Galois, O_L monogenic over O_K ([Se1] Prop. 12, p. 66)
imports: Krasner's lemma ([L] Lang, Algebraic Number Theory, p. 43)
proofSteps: 1.4: v_K(beta - g alpha) = min{i, i_{L/K}(g)} after conjugating beta, and P(beta) = prod_g (beta - g alpha).

1.5(i): lift the image of alpha to beta in O_E. Then v_K(P(beta)) >= m > u_{L/K}, so i = psi(v_K(P(beta))) > i_{L/K} and some g_0 has v_K(beta - g_0 alpha) > sup_{g != 1} v_K((g-1) g_0 alpha). Krasner's lemma gives g_0 alpha in K(beta) inside E.

1.5(ii): reduce to L/K totally ramified with alpha a uniformizer (P Eisenstein). The tame case uses a degree e_{L/K} - 1 extension. If p divides e_{L/K}, write e_{L/K} m = e_{L/K} r + s and perturb P to R = P - a X^s with v_K(a) = r; a root beta of R gives a homomorphism O_L -> O_E/a^m but no K-embedding, because e_{L/K} psi(m) = e_{L/K} u_{L/K} - d^{-1} would not be an integer.
acceptance: For L = Q_p(zeta_p) over Q_p (tamely and totally ramified), u_{L/K} = 1 by the tame case in the proof of 1.5(ii). So (P_m) holds for m > 1, and (ii) is consistent with (P_m) failing at m = 1 - 1/(p-1).

Alors : i) si m > u_{L/K}, (P_m) est vraie : ii) si (P_m) est vraie, m > u_{L/K} - e_{L/K}^{-1}.

nodes.title: Proposition 1.7(i): homomorphisms from a finite flat lci O_K-algebra B with Omega^1 free over B/a lift uniquely through aI for I with topologically nilpotent divided powers
nodes.statement: Let K have characteristic 0 and absolute ramification e = v_K(p). Let B be a finite flat O_K-algebra, locally a complete intersection, and suppose some a in O_K annihilates Omega^1_{B/O_K} with Omega^1_{B/O_K} a flat (B/a)-module. Let S be a finite flat O_K-algebra and I an ideal of S with divided powers that are topologically nilpotent (intersection of the I^[m] is 0). (a) For every O_K-homomorphism u : B -> S/aI there is a unique homomorphism utilde : B -> S such that u and utilde induce the same map B -> S/I. (b) The canonical map Hom_{O_K}(B, S) -> Hom_{O_K}(B, S/I) is injective. Example (1.6): for S = O_L, the ideal a^m_{L/K} has divided powers iff m >= e/(p-1), topologically nilpotent iff m > e/(p-1).
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0; B finite flat, locally complete intersection over O_K
a in O_K kills Omega^1_{B/O_K}, and Omega^1_{B/O_K} is (B/a)-flat
S finite flat over O_K; I with topologically nilpotent divided powers
proofSteps: Reduce to B local with residue field k. Omega^1_{B/O_K} is (B/a)-free with basis dx_1, ..., dx_h for x_j lifting a basis of m_B/(m_B^2 + m_K B). This identifies B with O_K[[X_1..X_h]]/J, J generated by P_1..P_h since B is finite lci.
From sum_j (dP_i/dX_j)(x) dx_j = 0 get dP_i/dX_j(x) = a p_ij with (p_ij) invertible in B (divide (q_li)(a p_ij) = a I_h by a, B being O_K-free).

Inductive step: given u : B -> S/aI^[n], a lift u' : B -> S/aI^[n+1] exists and is unique modulo I^[n+1]. With lifts u_i of u(x_i) and P_i(u) = a lambda_i, lambda_i in I^[n], one needs mu_j in I^[n] with P_i(u + mu) in aI^[n+1]. The Taylor expansion converges by topological nilpotence; higher derivatives of elements of J lie in a O_K[[X]] + J; so the conditions become lambda_i + sum_j p_ij(u) mu_j = 0 mod I^[n+1], solvable uniquely since (p_ij) is invertible.
(b) follows from the uniqueness in (a).
acceptance: Check the example 1.6 threshold m > e/(p-1) for S = O_L, which is where the e/(p-1) in the ramification bound comes from.

nodes.title: Proposition 1.7(ii): B_K is etale and the field L generated by the Kbar-points of B satisfies u_{L/K} <= v_K(a) + e/(p-1)
nodes.statement: In the situation of Proposition 1.7 (B finite flat lci over O_K, a killing Omega^1_{B/O_K} with Omega^1 flat over B/a), B_K = K (x) B is etale over K. If L is the smallest subfield of Kbar containing the images u(B) for all O_K-homomorphisms u : B -> Kbar, then L/K is Galois and u_{L/K} <= v_K(a) + e/(p-1).
hypotheses: as in Proposition 1.7
proofSteps: Omega^1_{B_K/K} = 0, so B_K = product of finite extensions L_s, and L is the compositum of their Galois closures. If a is a unit, B is etale over O_K and u_{L/K} = 0.

Assume a in m_K. For m > v_K(a) + e/(p-1), show (P_m). J(E) = Hom(B, O_E) has #J(E) <= #J(L), with equality iff L embeds in E. Given eta : O_L -> O_E/a^m_{E/K} = O_E/aI, where I has topologically nilpotent divided powers, map u -> u^eta by Proposition 1.7(i)(a).

Injectivity of u -> u^eta: embed the maximal unramified subextension compatibly. For alpha a uniformizer of O_L with minimal polynomial P over K', a lift beta of eta(alpha) has v_K(beta) = v_K(alpha) = 1/n. The kernel I' of O_L -> O_E/aI -> O_E/I is {x : v_K(x) >= m - v_K(a)}, which has topologically nilpotent divided powers, so injectivity follows from 1.7(i)(b).
By Proposition 1.5(ii), m > u_{L/K} - n^{-1} for all m > v_K(a) + e/(p-1), so u_{L/K} <= v_K(a) + e/(p-1) + 1/n.

Remove 1/n: if p does not divide n, L/K is tame and u_{L/K} = 1 <= v_K(a) + e/(p-1). If p divides n, n(p-1)u_{L/K} is an integer divisible by p, and so is n(p-1)v_K(a) + ne; hence n(p-1)u_{L/K} <= n(p-1)v_K(a) + ne.
acceptance: Check the tame case bound 1 <= v_K(a) + e/(p-1) uses a in m_K (v_K(a) >= 1).

nodes.title: Fontaine Theorem A / Theorem 1: for J finite flat over O_K killed by p^n, G^(u) acts trivially on J(Kbar) for u > e(n + 1/(p-1))
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field of characteristic p, e = v_K(p). Let n >= 1 and J a finite flat commutative group scheme over O_K killed by p^n, H the kernel of the action of G_K on J(Kbar), and L = Kbar^H. Then G_K^(u) is contained in H for every u > e(n + 1/(p-1)), where G^(u) = G^{u-1} in Serre's upper numbering.
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0, complete discretely valued, perfect residue field of characteristic p
J finite flat commutative over O_K, killed by p^n (n >= 1)

imports for the general case: Grothendieck's embedding of J into a Barsotti-Tate group ([BBM] Berthelot-Breen-Messing or [I] Illusie); for case (a): structure of the special fibre ([De] Demazure, Lectures on p-divisible groups, Ch. II) and Omega^1_{B/O_K} = B (x) omega_J ([Fo] n. 4.3)
proofSteps: Reduce to k algebraically closed. Let B be the affine algebra of J and omega_J the module of invariant differentials (primitive elements of Omega^1_{B/O_K}).

(a) omega_J free over O_K/p^n: J_k is the product of an etale group and a connected group whose algebra is k[X_1..X_h]/(X_1^{p^{r_1}}, ..., X_h^{p^{r_h}}) ([De] Ch. II), so B_k and hence B is a local complete intersection. Omega^1_{B/O_K} = B (x) omega_J ([Fo] n. 4.3) is free over B/p^n. Apply Proposition 1.7 and Corollary 1.8 with a = p^n (v_K(a) = ne).

(b) General case: J embeds in a Barsotti-Tate group Gamma ([BBM] or [I]), so J(Kbar) is in Gamma_{p^n}(Kbar) and it suffices to treat Gamma_{p^n}. The fppf sequence 0 -> Gamma_{p^n} -> Gamma -> Gamma -> 0 gives 0 -> omega_Gamma -> omega_Gamma -> omega_{Gamma_{p^n}} -> 0; omega_Gamma is O_K-free, so omega_{Gamma_{p^n}} is free over O_K/p^n and (a) applies.
Remark 2.2(a): for e = n = 1, O_K/p = k and omega_J is automatically free, so the Barsotti-Tate embedding is unnecessary.
acceptance: Translate to Serre's numbering: G^v acts trivially for v > e(n + 1/(p-1)) - 1.
Remark 2.2(b) (conjectural bounds u_{n,i} <= e(n + i/(p-1)) for H^i of proper smooth schemes) is explicitly a conjecture ("il me semble raisonnable de conjecturer") and is not a theorem target.
Remark 2.2(c): Sen's theorem gives e(n + c') <= u_n <= e(n + c) for p-adic representations; for Tate modules of Barsotti-Tate groups Theorem 1 gives c = 1/(p-1).

nodes.title: Raynaud Lemma 4.2.3: a connected p-divisible group over a field of characteristic p deforms over k[[T]] to one that is ordinary at the generic point
nodes.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0 and X a connected p-divisible group over k. Then X deforms to a p-divisible group over k[[T]] that is of ordinary type (an extension of an etale group by a group of multiplicative type) above the generic point.
hypotheses: k a field of characteristic p
imports: Cartier's theory of typical curves ([1], [2], and especially Mumford, Bi-extensions of formal groups [9])
proofSteps: Let T be the A(k)-module of typical curves of X (A(L) = W(L)[[F, V]]), e_1..e_d a basis of T/VT = Lie(X), m_i lifts, and Q_ij in W(k)[[V]] with F(m_i) = sum_j Q_ij m_j.

Over L = k[[T]] choose arbitrary lifts Qtilde_ij in W(L)[[V]] and let Ttilde be A(L)^d modulo the F m_i - sum Qtilde_ij m_j; it is the module of typical curves of a formal group Xtilde over k[[T]] lifting X, with p-Lie algebra free of rank d and p-power map induced by F.
Choose the lifts so that the p-power map on Lie(Xtilde) (x) k((T)) is injective; then the Lie algebra is generically of multiplicative type, i.e. Xtilde is generically ordinary.
acceptance: The literature on typical curves is "bien incomplete" (Raynaud); record the import boundary rather than treating this as elementary.

nodes.title: Raynaud Theorem 4.2.1: for a p-divisible group X of height h and dimension d over a strictly henselian mixed-characteristic R, Galois acts on det T(X) by tau^d
nodes.statement: Let R be a strictly henselian DVR of mixed characteristic (0, p), tau : Gal(Kbar/K) -> Z_p^* the character on T(mu_{p^infinity}), and X an R-p-divisible group of height h and dimension d with Tate module T(X) of X (x)_R K. Then Gal(Kbar/K) acts on det T(X) = Lambda^h T(X) through tau^d. Remark 4.2.2: Tate had shown, using Hodge-Tate decompositions, that the two characters agree on an open subgroup.
hypotheses: R strictly henselian discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) (no bound on e)
X a p-divisible group over R of height h and dimension d

imports: unobstructedness of deformations of p-divisible groups (Lazard, Cartier, Grothendieck, via [2]), so the versal deformation ring O is a power series ring over R; Zariski-Nagata purity ([6] SGA 2, p. 118)
proofSteps: Assume R complete (the Galois group is unchanged) and, by devissage, Xbar = X (x)_R k connected. The ordinary case (etale by multiplicative) is evident.
Let O be the complete local ring of a versal deformation of Xbar over R, a power series algebra over R, S = Spec O regular, and Xcal the universal deformation.

By Lemma 4.2.3, Xcal is ordinary above the generic point x of Sbar = S (x)_R k. Dimension is preserved under deformation in characteristic p, so over a strict henselization Stilde at x, Xcal is an extension of (Q_p/Z_p)^{h-d} by (mu_{p^infinity})^d.

Hence Lambda^h T(Xcal) (x) T(mu_{p^infinity})^{(x) -d} is unramified at x. It is also unramified at the characteristic-zero points of S (x) K, hence at all codimension <= 1 points of S, and by Zariski-Nagata purity it is unramified on S.
Restricting to a suitable section of S over R shows Lambda^h T(X) (x) T(mu_{p^infinity})^{(x) -d} is unramified over R, hence trivial because R is strictly henselian.
acceptance: X = mu_{p^infinity} (h = d = 1): det T = T(mu_{p^infinity}), character tau^1.
X = Q_p/Z_p (h = 1, d = 0): trivial character, tau^0.
Consequence (Remark 4.1.2): the determinant formula of Theorem 4.1.1 holds for p-kernels of p-divisible groups without the hypothesis e <= p-1.

nodes.title: Witt covectors CW_k(R), their F, V and W(k)-module structure, and the Dieudonne ring D_k = W(k)[F, V] (statement level; proofs in Fontaine, Asterisque 47-48)
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect of characteristic p. For a finite k-algebra R, CW_k(R) is the set of sequences a = (..., a_{-n}, ..., a_0) of elements of R indexed by non-positive integers with a_i nilpotent for i large; addition is c_{-n} = lim_m S_m(a_{-n-m}, ..., a_{-n}, b_{-n-m}, ..., b_{-n}) (a stationary limit), using the Witt addition polynomials S_m. CW_k(R) is a commutative topological group (as a subset of the product of discrete copies of R) with a unique compatible topological W(k)-module structure satisfying [x] . a = (..., x^{p^{-n}} a_{-n}, ..., x^{p^{-1}} a_{-1}, a_0). F(a) = (..., a_{-n}^p, ..., a_0^p) and V(a) = (..., a_{-n-1}, ..., a_{-1}) are additive, continuous, F V = V F = p, F is sigma-semilinear and V sigma^{-1}-semilinear. Hence CW_k(R) is a topological module over D_k = W(k)[F, V] with F V = V F = p, F alpha = sigma(alpha) F, V alpha = sigma^{-1}(alpha) V. For R = k' a finite extension of k, CW_k(k') = K'/W(k') with K' = Frac W(k'). The functor CW_k on finite k-algebras is pro-represented by a formal affine commutative k-group scheme CWhat_k. Fontaine-Laffaille 9.1 give the same objects for a W(k)-algebra with the nilpotence condition (psi).
hypotheses: k perfect of characteristic p > 0
R a finite k-algebra (more general topological rings require care, Conrad p. 4)
proofSteps: Source status: Conrad's "Summary of some results of Fontaine" recalls these facts with references to Fontaine, Groupes p-divisibles sur les corps locaux [7]: Ch. II, Prop. 1.4 (group structure), pp. 79-82 (F, V, W(k)-module), Ch. II Section 4.2 (pro-representability), Ch. II Section 2.3 (general topological rings). The proofs were not read; Asterisque 47-48 is not in the library.
acceptance: Check CW_k(k) = K_0/W(k) with F acting as sigma and V as p sigma^{-1}.

nodes.title: Fontaine's Dieudonne theory: M(G) = Hom(G, CWhat_k) gives an anti-equivalence from finite commutative p-group schemes over perfect k to D_k-modules of finite W(k)-length (statement level)
nodes.statement: Let k be perfect of characteristic p. For a p-formal commutative group scheme G over k (G = lim G[p^n], e.g. a finite commutative k-group scheme of p-power order or a p-divisible group), the Dieudonne module is M(G) = Hom(G, CWhat_k), a topological D_k-module. For a finite commutative p-group J over k, M(J) is identified with the D_k-submodule of covectors (..., x_{-n}, ..., x_0) in CW(O(J)) with (..., m^* x_{-n}, ..., m^* x_0) = (..., x_{-n} (x) 1, ..., x_0 (x) 1) + (..., 1 (x) x_{-n}, ..., 1 (x) x_0) (primitive covectors). The functor M is an anti-equivalence of abelian categories between p-formal commutative group schemes over k and a category of topological D_k-modules. In particular it is a contravariant anti-equivalence between finite commutative p-group schemes over k and finite D_k-modules (finite W(k)-length).
hypotheses: k perfect of characteristic p

nodes.title: Raynaud's Example: for a supersingular elliptic curve over an absolutely unramified strictly henselian base, E[p] is a simple F_{p^2}-vector space scheme X^{p^2} = pX with inertia character a fundamental character of level 2
nodes.statement: Let R be a strictly henselian DVR of mixed characteristic, absolutely unramified (e = 1), and Ecal an elliptic curve over R whose special fibre has Hasse invariant zero. Let Gcal = Ecal[p] and G its generic fibre; Gcal is finite flat of rank q = p^2. (a) G is a simple group scheme. (b) G is an F-vector space scheme with F of p^2 elements; Gcal itself is an R-scheme in F-vector spaces, with an equation X^{p^2} = pX. The character psi : mu_{p^2-1}(K) -> F^* describing the Galois action on G(Kbar) is one of the fundamental characters psi_i of level 2.
hypotheses: R strictly henselian, mixed characteristic, e = 1
Ecal/R elliptic curve with supersingular (Hasse invariant zero) special fibre
proofSteps: (a) If G were not simple, it would contain a subgroup scheme H of rank p. The schematic closure of H in Gcal would be etale or of multiplicative type (a rank-p F_p-vector space scheme has exponent 0 or e = 1, Corollary 1.5.2). That contradicts Hasse invariant zero, since the special fibre is then connected with connected dual.

(b) G simple implies G is an F-vector space scheme with #F = q = p^2 (Proposition 3.2.1). Then Gcal is an R-scheme in F-vector spaces (Proposition 3.3.2: uniqueness for e < p-1, or the e = p-1 case 3o for p = 2). It has an equation X^{p^2} = pX, and Theorem 3.4.1 gives psi = psi_i.

Unwritten detail: in Corollary 1.5.1 with r = 2, the equation X_1^{p^2} = delta_1^p delta_2 X_1 with valuation 1 forces (v(delta_1), v(delta_2)) = (0, 1) up to the cyclic shift. So psi = psi_{i+1}^0 psi_{i+2}^1, a single fundamental character.
acceptance: Consequence for R07.5: over an absolutely unramified base, the tame inertia action on E[p] of a supersingular elliptic curve with good reduction is a single fundamental character of level 2 on the F_{p^2}-line E[p](Kbar), i.e. the pair of conjugate level-2 fundamental characters on the underlying F_p-plane.
The ordinary case (connected-etale sequence of E[p] with multiplicative connected part) is not in this source; see the R07.5 gap.
